In contrast, ISpyU models fine-tuned on real target-phone data drop to 25.9% word accuracy on unseen phones; CamEar improves cross-device accuracy by 101.4% and outperforms ISpyU's same-device models on every tested phone.
tldr: The paper shows that Android's Camera2 HAL metadata exposes high-rate gyroscope streams (up to 800-1000 Hz) that leak loudspeaker speech, and introduces a simulation-trained recognizer (CamEar) that generalizes across unseen phones.
motivation: Android 12+ throttles motion sensors to 200 Hz to block sensor-based covert microphoning, but the authors ask whether other subsystems can bypass these privacy defenses and enable zero-permission acoustic eavesdropping.
method: They survey 50 smartphones from 10 vendors for Camera2 CaptureResult gyroscope metadata exposure and sampling rates, then build Source-to-Leakage Learning (S2L), a physics-constrained forward simulator that decouples speech content from device-specific mechanical resonances so a recognizer can be trained without target-phone traces.
result: 37 of 50 phones expose gyroscope metadata via Camera2 and 26 exceed 200 Hz (six flagships at 800-1000 Hz), bypassing mic/camera toggles; CamEar reaches 52.1% mean word accuracy (up to 61.8%) and 74.3% character accuracy on unseen 800-1000 Hz phones, versus 25.9% word accuracy for fine-tuned ISpyU baselines on unseen devices.
conclusion: Camera2 metadata constitutes an unguarded high-rate side channel that defeats current Android sensor-throttling defenses, and simulation-based domain generalization substantially improves cross-device attack transferability, motivating tighter metadata-rate restrictions.

title: Dissipative Erasure Of Pulse-to-pulse Dispersion Imbalance In Ultrafast Burst-mode Lasers
authors: Mesut La\c{c}in, Paul Repgen, Umut Aydemir, Fatih \"omer Ilday
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrafast GHz bursts enable laser-matter interactions where successive excitations collectively build sustained nonequilibrium states and efficient material interactions. However, directly generating pulse trains at GHz rates remains challenging. Alternatively, repetition-rate multipliers (RRMs) divide each oscillator pulse into equidistant replicas, but either suffer from dispersion imbalances that prevent simultaneous compression or are limited to few pulses per burst. Here, we introduce dissipative erasure, which first suppresses the differences by spectral filtering and then regenerates the optical bandwidth via nonlinear amplification without restoring the erased differences. We derive two scaling results: as the repetition rate increases geometrically with RRM stages, maximum path differences approach a finite limit; meanwhile, dispersive differences weaken quadratically with filtering. We demonstrate dissipative erasure experimentally, generating 100-[MATH]J bursts, comprising thousands of 100-fs pulses at 51.3 GHz, from a Yb-fiber amplifier. Dissipative erasure has diverse potential applications for suppressing deterministic or stochastic differences before recovering desired optical properties.
tldr: The paper introduces 'dissipative erasure,' a spectral-filtering-plus-nonlinear-amplification technique to remove pulse-to-pulse dispersion imbalance in GHz burst-mode ultrafast fiber lasers, demonstrated with 100-µJ bursts of thousands of 100-fs pulses at 51.3 GHz.
motivation: Repetition-rate multipliers can split oscillator pulses into GHz pulse trains, but dispersion imbalances between replicas prevent simultaneous compression and limit the number of pulses per burst.
method: Dispersion differences among replicas are first suppressed by spectral filtering, then the optical bandwidth is regenerated through nonlinear amplification without restoring the erased differences; scaling laws for path differences and dispersive differences versus number of RRM stages are derived.
result: Two scaling results are obtained (maximum path differences saturate geometrically with stage number; dispersive differences weaken quadratically with filtering), and 100-µJ bursts containing thousands of 100-fs pulses at 51.3 GHz are generated from a Yb-fiber amplifier.
conclusion: Dissipative erasure provides a general means of suppressing deterministic or stochastic pulse-to-pulse differences before recovering desired optical properties, with potential applications across ultrafast laser-matter interaction regimes.

title: Pushy Random Walk On The Bethe Lattice: A Galton-Watson Perspective
authors: J\'er\'emie Klinger
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pushy random walks are minimal models of transport in deformable media, in which the walker displaces the obstacles it bumps into rather than being blocked by them. On the Bethe lattice, we show that the walkable structure dynamically created by a pushy walker can be generated a priori as an explicit multi-type Galton-Watson tree, so that the walker reduces to a simple random walk on a static random tree, and its escape to infinity coincides with the survival of the underlying branching process. Standard generating-function tools then give direct access to the escape properties of these walks. For the Sokoban walk, which pushes a single obstacle, we recover the known critical density [MATH] and the behavior of the escape probability close to [MATH], and derive its small-density asymptotics. For the second-order pushy walk, which can push trains of two obstacles, we establish the conjectured [MATH], and compute the escape probability at all densities. Beyond escape, the same framework yields the statistics of the trace of trapped walkers: the distribution of the maximal depth follows from the extinction probabilities, while the distributions of the visited volume and of the number of dead ends are encoded in explicit functional equations for their generating functions, which we invert numerically. All predictions agree with Monte Carlo simulations.
tldr: The paper maps a pushy random walk (a walker that displaces obstacles) on the Bethe lattice onto a simple random walk on a static multi-type Galton-Watson tree, which lets the escape problem be solved with standard branching-process generating functions.
motivation: Pushy random walks are minimal models of transport in deformable media, but their escape properties on the Bethe lattice are known only in special cases; a cleaner formalism is needed to compute escape probabilities and the statistics of trapped walkers.
method: The dynamically generated walkable structure is constructed a priori as an explicit multi-type Galton-Watson tree, reducing the process to a random walk on a static random tree whose survival equals escape to infinity; generating-function and functional-equation techniques then yield escape and trap statistics, checked against Monte Carlo simulation.
result: For the Sokoban walk (single-obstacle pushing) the known critical density and near-critical escape-probability behaviour are recovered along with small-density asymptotics; for the second-order pushy walk the conjectured critical density is established and the escape probability is computed at all densities, plus distributions of maximal depth, visited volume, and dead ends for trapped walkers.
conclusion: The Galton-Watson encoding provides a unified and tractable framework for escape and trapping statistics of pushy random walks, with all analytic predictions confirmed by simulation.

title: Ultrafast Imaging Of Ring Currents In Atoms And Condensed Matter By Electron Scattering
authors: Zhongchen Xing, Xinbao Liu, Peixiang Lu, Eberhard K. U. Gross, Zheng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ring currents are well known to generate magnetic fields. Despite the rich phenomena and detection of the ring current, an experimental reconstruction of the ring current at the atomic scale is still unsolved. In this work, we propose a method of resolving the ring current in a sample at the atomic scale by ultrafast electron diffraction. Inspired by the Rosenbluth formula, we study the electron diffraction of a sample with a ring current and separate the scattering cross sections into three kinds of response functions, which stand for the electric part, the magnetic part and the cross term, respectively. The ring current in the sample can be reconstructed from measuring the response function in different scattering configurations. Also, following the Rosenbluth formula, we propose that the response functions can be measured by fitting over fixed momentum transfer with different incident energy and relative direction, which is similar to the [MATH]-scan in crystal diffraction. With high-precision ultrafast electron diffraction, the magnetic part will be resolved despite being much weaker than the electric part. We simulate three examples with ring currents -- an ideal hydrogen atom, a circularly polarized helium atom ensemble, and a lithium crystal. Our model offers a promising way to resolve the current structure at the atomic scale.
tldr: The paper proposes ultrafast electron diffraction as a method to reconstruct ring currents in atoms and condensed matter at atomic scale.
motivation: Ring currents generate magnetic fields but atomic-scale experimental reconstruction remains unsolved, motivating a scattering-based imaging approach.
method: Inspired by the Rosenbluth formula, the authors separate electron scattering cross sections into electric, magnetic, and cross-term response functions and propose extracting them via measurements at different incident energies and directions.
result: Simulations for an ideal hydrogen atom, circularly polarized helium ensemble, and lithium crystal show that the magnetic response, though weak, can be resolved with high-precision ultrafast electron diffraction.
conclusion: The model offers a promising route to resolve current structure at atomic scale, but it is outside the four targeted quantum-information research directions.

title: The Garnett--Jones Distance Theorem For Rectangles
authors: Hrvoje Sikic Morten Nielsen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the family of all axis-parallel rectangles in [MATH], [MATH], we characterize the distance of a real- or complex-valued function of rectangular bounded mean oscillation (little bmo) to [MATH] by the reciprocal of its critical exponential integrability exponent. For each [MATH] at which the rectangular exponential moment of [MATH] is finite, we construct a bounded correction so that the residual has mean absolute oscillation bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times [MATH] on every rectangle. The proof bounds products of coordinate maximal operators between two sets in terms of the supremum of their density product over common test rectangles. Selecting a longest interval along each path lets us remove repeated visits to a coordinate, so the density exponent is independent of the number of factors. The maximal-operator estimate holds with every positive density exponent below [MATH] in two dimensions and below [MATH] in three dimensions.
tldr: This paper proves a Garnett-Jones distance theorem for little bmo functions on axis-parallel rectangles, characterizing distance to L-infinity via critical exponential integrability.
motivation: The work addresses a pure harmonic analysis problem concerning bounded mean oscillation on product domains and exponential integrability exponents.
method: The proof constructs bounded corrections using bounds on products of coordinate maximal operators, controlled by density products over common test rectangles and a longest-interval selection argument.
result: The authors characterize the distance of a function in little bmo to L-infinity by the reciprocal of its critical exponential integrability exponent, with maximal-operator estimates in two and three dimensions.
conclusion: The result advances rectangle-adapted bmo theory and maximal operator estimates, but it has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Littlestone Dimension And Its Dual
authors: Chavdar Lalov Pooya Hatami
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class [MATH], [MATH], is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class [MATH], obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that [MATH] and [MATH] are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound [MATH]. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the improved bound \[ ()\le 2^{O(^*()^2)}. \] An exponential dependence is necessary, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.
tldr: The paper improves the quantitative bound relating the Littlestone dimension of a concept class to that of its dual class, showing a doubly-exponential separation is not necessary.
motivation: Shelah's classical result establishes that the Littlestone dimension and its dual are simultaneously finite, and Hodges' 1981 work gave a doubly exponential bound; Malliaris and Moran asked whether that bound is optimal.
method: Combinatorial analysis of concept classes and their duals, using model-theoretic and learning-theoretic techniques to bound the dual Littlestone dimension in terms of the Littlestone dimension.
result: They prove the improved bound Ldim(C*) ≤ 2^{O(Ldim(C)^2)}, and construct the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain to show an exponential dependence is unavoidable.
conclusion: The doubly exponential bound of Hodges is not optimal; the true relationship is singly exponential, resolving the question of Malliaris and Moran.

title: Learning Under Bounded Manipulation For Quadratic Incentive Design
authors: Arda G\"u\c{c}l\"u, Subhonmesh Bose, Tamer Ba\c{s}ar
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a repeated quadratic incentive design game in which a leader learns a follower's private type from noisy observations of the follower's actions and uses her estimates in an affine incentive rule. The follower knows the leader's learning policy, which incorporates past observations to produce estimates of the follower's type, and can deviate from his myopic best response to influence the leader's future estimates. We ask how the follower's ability to manipulate these observations affects the leader's performance. Under a manipulation budget [MATH] constraining the expected cumulative squared deviation of the follower's actions from his myopic best response, we establish a minimax regret rate of order [MATH] for approximately rational followers. Our information-theoretic lower bound applies to a general class of causal estimation and manipulation policies for the leader and the follower. We provide a simple learning policy that achieves the lower bound. Finally, we show that under a fixed learning rule, increasing the manipulation budget of the follower can counterintuitively reduce the leader's regret.
tldr: The paper studies repeated quadratic incentive design where a follower can manipulate the leader's noisy learning of his private type under a bounded manipulation budget.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how strategic manipulation of observations affects a leader's regret in learning-based incentive design.
method: They formulate a minimax regret problem for approximately rational followers under a cumulative squared-deviation manipulation budget and derive an information-theoretic lower bound for causal estimation and manipulation policies.
result: They establish a minimax regret rate of order sqrt(M) and provide a learning policy that achieves the lower bound; they also show that increasing the follower's manipulation budget can sometimes reduce the leader's regret.
conclusion: The work characterizes fundamental limits of learning in strategic environments with bounded manipulation, but it is a classical game-theory/online-learning contribution unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Felid: A Flexible And Efficient Design For Transformer Fine-Tuning Over Encrypted Data
authors: Linru Zhang, Jun Jie Sim, Xiangning Wang, Jiahao Zhong, Kaiyu Zhou, Huanyi Ye, Yongsen Zheng, Lushan Song, Xiaojian Liang, Yingting Liu, Yujing Sun, Huaxiong Wang, Pu Duan, Kwok-Yan Lam
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables non-interactive, privacy-preserving transformer fine-tuning, protecting highly sensitive data as inputs to large language models. Prior work has predominantly pursued efficiency gains through architectural refinements, yet overall performance remains bounded by the substantial cost inherent in encrypted computation. To address these issues, we target the bottleneck at the ciphertext operation level. Concretely, we propose a novel packing strategy that supports batching over a flexible number of inputs, making it well-suited for fine-tuning workloads. In addition, we design operation-specific matrix evaluation algorithms that significantly reduce (i) the number of ciphertext rotations and relinearizations, and (ii) the number of bootstrapping invocations. Additionally, we exploit functional bootstrapping to fold the evaluation of element-wise activation functions directly into the bootstrapping step, thereby reducing overall computational complexity. As a result, our framework achieves a [MATH] reduction in ciphertext rotations and relinearizations across all matrix operations, as well as a [MATH] reduction in FHE bootstrapping invocations over the entire computation flow, compared to the latest state-of-the-art work. It is worth noting that our system completes fine-tuning of a 2-layer BERT-style model with a batch size of 16 in 650 seconds, achieving a [MATH] speedup over the state-of-the-art work.
tldr: Felid is a fully homomorphic encryption framework that accelerates privacy-preserving transformer fine-tuning through improved packing, operation-specific matrix evaluation, and functional bootstrapping for activations.
motivation: FHE enables non-interactive privacy-preserving fine-tuning of large language models on sensitive data, but ciphertext-level computational costs remain prohibitive despite architectural refinements in prior work.
method: The authors introduce a flexible packing strategy supporting batching over variable input counts, operation-specific matrix evaluation algorithms that cut ciphertext rotations, relinearizations, and bootstrapping calls, and fold element-wise activation functions into functional bootstrapping.
result: The framework reports asymptotic-order reductions in rotations/relinearizations across all matrix operations and in bootstrapping invocations over the full computation flow, fine-tuning a 2-layer BERT-style model with batch size 16 in 650 seconds and a large speedup over the state of the art.
conclusion: Targeting the ciphertext-operation bottleneck yields substantial practical speedups for encrypted transformer fine-tuning, making FHE-based private training more viable.

title: Simple Routes To Turing-Like Patterns
authors: Zhan Zhao, Xiang-Ning Li, Wen-Wen Li, Ji-Chong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spots, stripes, and networks recur in systems with very different microscopic dynamics, suggesting that the competing processes behind Turing-like patterns may be easy to realise. We ask whether local amplification coupled to suppression over a wider region can generate these geometries in simple systems beyond chemical reaction--diffusion models. We test this idea in two settings, a binary cellular automaton obtained by adding a distant neighbour count to Conway's Game of Life and a self-gravitating toy universe described by particle motion and two continuous fields. The automaton produces spots, stripes, and coexistence across its control plane, while a rule retaining only the two opposing counts produces islands, stripes, and holes. Directional correlations and intrinsic dimension identify the same region of orientational order. In the gravitational system, convergence increases local density while mass transport depletes the surroundings. The two-field and particle densities have a smoothed spatial correlation of [MATH] at scale factor [MATH] under the original force law, and strengthening its long-wavelength component drives both descriptions toward fewer dense condensations. Together, these results show how simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realise competing growth and suppression, providing two concrete routes by which Turing-like geometries can recur across different dynamics.
tldr: The paper explores simple mechanisms for generating Turing-like patterns using a modified Game of Life automaton and a self-gravitating toy universe.
motivation: Turing-like patterns appear across diverse systems, motivating a search for simple generic mechanisms based on local amplification and wider suppression beyond chemical reaction-diffusion models.
method: The authors test two settings: a binary cellular automaton extending Conway's Game of Life with a distant-neighbor count, and a self-gravitating toy universe with particle motion and two continuous fields.
result: The automaton produces spots, stripes, coexistence, islands, and holes depending on control parameters; the gravitational system shows smoothed spatial correlations and fewer dense condensations when long-wavelength forces are strengthened.
conclusion: Simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realize competing growth and suppression, providing concrete routes for Turing-like geometries to recur across different dynamics.

title: Multiconfigurational And Spin-Orbit Extensions Of The Bsr-rmt Interface
authors: Aaron T. Bondy, Juan C. Del Valle, Kathryn R. Hamilton, Klaus Bartschat
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the extension of the B-spline R-matrix (BSR) to R-matrix with time dependence (RMT) interface to include support for multiconfiguration target states and [MATH] coupling, including the one-body spin-orbit (SO) interaction. Inner-region input data generated by BSR are transformed through the interface for time propagation in RMT. Two examples demonstrate the working interface: high-order harmonic generation in helium and weak-field, near-resonance response in carbon. The helium comparisons employ previously studied laser parameters, displaying excellent agreement with the established Belfast R-matrix input codes in the time-dependent dipole and harmonic spectrum, both with and without SO. Further structure comparisons in helium show close agreement in the SO-induced changes in energy and oscillator strengths. The two codes coincide on the much larger SO-induced change in the dipole response in carbon, demonstrating agreement for multiconfigurational target states. These extensions allow the flexibility of BSR structure calculations to be used in time-dependent studies of heavier and more complex atoms.
tldr: The paper extends the BSR-to-RMT interface to support multiconfigurational target states and spin-orbit coupling for time-dependent atomic calculations.
motivation: Time-dependent R-matrix calculations for heavier and more complex atoms require flexible multiconfigurational structure input and spin-orbit effects, which the existing BSR-RMT interface lacked.
method: The authors upgrade the BSR-RMT interface to transform multiconfiguration and spin-orbit BSR inner-region data for RMT time propagation, validating it with helium high-harmonic generation and near-resonant carbon response calculations.
result: The extended interface agrees closely with established Belfast R-matrix input codes for helium dipole and harmonic spectra, with and without spin-orbit coupling, and reproduces the large spin-orbit-induced dipole response change in carbon.
conclusion: The new capabilities enable time-dependent studies of heavier and more complex atomic systems using BSR structure calculations within RMT.

title: Sop Sensing In Hollow-Core Fiber: Forward Sensing Using Cots Transponder And Localization With Coherent Otdr
authors: Adrish Sahu, Rajiv Boddeda, Arnaud Dupas, Carina Castineiras Carrero, Ha\"ik Mardoyan, Sterenn Guerrier, Matteo Lonardi, Javier Errea Moreno, Peng Li, Shuhai Li, Lei Zhang, Jie Luo, Daniel Peterson, J\'er\'emie Renaudier
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We experimentally investigate and compare distributed state-of-polarization sensing in support-tube hollow-core and standard single-mode fiber. Despite significantly weaker Rayleigh backscattering and reduced polarization sensitivity in hollow-core fiber, polarization perturbations remain observable and spatially localizable, demonstrating the feasibility of SOP-based distributed sensing in hollow-core fiber.
tldr: The paper experimentally compares distributed state-of-polarization sensing in hollow-core fiber versus standard single-mode fiber using a commercial transponder and coherent OTDR localization.
motivation: The authors aim to assess whether polarization-based distributed sensing remains feasible in hollow-core fiber despite its weaker Rayleigh backscattering and reduced polarization sensitivity.
method: They perform forward state-of-polarization sensing with a COTS transponder and localize polarization perturbations using coherent optical time-domain reflectometry in both hollow-core and standard single-mode fiber.
result: Polarization perturbations in hollow-core fiber are observable and spatially localizable, though the sensitivity is lower than in standard single-mode fiber.
conclusion: SOP-based distributed sensing in hollow-core fiber is experimentally feasible, but the work is a classical fiber-sensing demonstration with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid quantum systems contribution.

title: On A Supersymmetric Generalization Of The Matytsin Formula
authors: Evgeny Porubov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup [MATH] in the limit [MATH] when [MATH] is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for [MATH]. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.
tldr: The paper derives the leading asymptotic behavior of a supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for a supergroup, generalizing Matytsin's formula.
motivation: The work aims to extend known asymptotic results for matrix integrals, specifically the Matytsin formula, to supersymmetric settings involving supergroups.
method: The authors compute the leading asymptotics of a supersymmetric Itzykson-Zuber integral in a large parameter limit with another parameter finite, using classical Hamiltonian actions.
result: They show that the asymptotics are described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to bosonic and fermionic sectors.
conclusion: The result provides a supersymmetric generalization of the Matytsin formula and links its asymptotics to bosonic and fermionic Hamiltonian dynamics.

title: Composite Dielectric-Loaded Metallic Metagratings For Dual-Polarized Transmissive Beam Manipulation
authors: Vitali Specktor, Yuval Singer, Ilya Varenisov, Ariel Epstein
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present and experimentally demonstrate a comprehensive analytical suite for the design of transmissive metal-based metagratings (MGs) for dual-polarized anomalous refraction. Considering a composite configuration of perforated metallic slabs with controlled dielectric loading, we develop a rigorous mode-matching formulation tying the various MG degrees of freedom to the various reflected and transmitted Floquet-Bloch modes, enabling efficient beam deflection for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations. Inherently versatile, the analytical framework accurately models single-layer and double-layer constructs with multiple rectangular perforations per unit cell, each potentially loaded with dielectric material. We harness this degree-of-freedom abundance to devise diverse polarization-sensitive transmissive MGs, ranging from all-metallic single-layer and double-layer structures for single-polarized (TM or TE) perfect anomalous refraction, to dielectric-loaded architectures implementing dual-polarized routing of the incident wave. Beyond highlighting concrete paths to address TE-polarized fields in such formations, our results, validated via full-wave simulations and experiments at K band, showcase the great potential of metal-based MGs for manipulating fields in transmission, facilitating effective synthesis of durable dual-polarized beamforming superstrates for environmentally demanding and high power antenna applications.
tldr: The paper presents an analytical and experimental framework for designing transmissive metal-based metagratings with dielectric loading for dual-polarized beam deflection.
motivation: The authors aim to enable durable, high-power, polarization-sensitive beamforming superstrates using metal-based metagratings rather than purely dielectric or reconfigurable metasurfaces.
method: They develop a rigorous mode-matching formulation for perforated metallic slabs with controlled dielectric loading, modeling single- and double-layer constructs with multiple rectangular perforations per unit cell.
result: The framework is validated by full-wave simulations and K-band experiments, demonstrating single-polarized perfect anomalous refraction and dual-polarized routing in dielectric-loaded architectures.
conclusion: Metal-based metagratings with dielectric loading are shown to be versatile for transmissive beam manipulation, offering a path toward robust dual-polarized antenna applications.

title: Hall Effect In Electrolyte Solutions: Self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager Theory
authors: Nikolai Kalikin Yury Budkov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A self-consistent statistical-mechanical theory of the Hall effect in electrolyte solutions is developed by extending the self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager (SCDHO) framework to crossed electric and magnetic fields. The theory incorporates non-local ionic charge distributions through Slater-type form factors and ion-specific coefficients describing the effective Lorentz response, with experimental input for protons and hydroxide ions. Within the random-phase approximation, the Hall conductivity is expressed as mean-field, correlation, and electrophoretic contributions. Both interaction channels include the Lorentz rotation of the complete electric-field-induced ionic velocity. In the point-charge limit with hydrodynamics suppressed, the relaxation correction agrees with independent odd stochastic density functional theory and the relaxation part of Friedman's classical result. For 22 dilute aqueous electrolytes, the mean absolute relative deviations from measured Hall constants and Hall numbers are about 17 percent. At finite concentrations, the theory predicts a nonmonotonic Hall number for NaBPh4 and sign changes of the electrophoretic correction for NaI and HCl. Correlation effects dominate for HCl and LiOH, whereas the two interaction channels become comparable for KOH and aqueous imidazolium salts. The results clarify how ionic mobilities, effective Hall coefficients, charge distributions, and solvent hydrodynamics determine electrolyte magnetotransport.
tldr: The paper develops a self-consistent statistical-mechanical theory of the Hall effect in electrolyte solutions by extending the Debye-Hückel-Onsager framework to crossed electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify how ionic mobilities, effective Hall coefficients, charge distributions, and solvent hydrodynamics determine magnetotransport in dilute and finite-concentration electrolytes.
method: They incorporate non-local ionic charge distributions via Slater-type form factors and ion-specific Lorentz-response coefficients, expressing Hall conductivity within the random-phase approximation as mean-field, correlation, and electrophoretic contributions.
result: For 22 dilute aqueous electrolytes, the theory gives mean absolute relative deviations of about 17% from measured Hall constants and Hall numbers, and predicts nonmonotonic Hall numbers and sign changes at finite concentration.
conclusion: The SCDHO extension provides a self-consistent framework for electrolyte magnetotransport, but it is a classical statistical-mechanical theory of ionic solutions with no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method For Uncertain Particle Systems With Singularities
authors: Wenyi Wang, Lei Li, Yiwen Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.
tldr: The paper introduces a stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) numerical method for simulating uncertain particle systems whose drift and diffusion coefficients contain singularities.
motivation: Particle systems with uncertain coefficients and singular drift/diffusion terms cause numerical blow-up in existing schemes, so a more robust solver is needed.
method: The authors combine an exponential regularization (taming) strategy that keeps stochastic Galerkin projection coefficients finite with a random batch approach to reduce computational complexity for large-scale simulations.
result: Theoretical properties of the algorithm are established, and numerical tests show weak convergence, lower errors than existing methods on singular tests, and stability over a wider range of singular regimes.
conclusion: The str-RB method provides a robust and accurate foundation for high-performance solvers of uncertain many-body particle dynamics.

title: Strong Numerical Radius Orthogonality On Bounded Linear Operators
authors: Shaoxing Sun (air Force Engineering University), Xiaofei Qi (shanxi University), Jinchuan Hou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthogonality is an important tool for studying bounded linear operators. In this paper, we introduce the concept of strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators and then, discuss the properties about numerical radius orthogonality, strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators as well as relationship between them.
tldr: The paper introduces a notion of strong numerical radius orthogonality for bounded linear operators and studies its properties and relation to numerical radius orthogonality.
motivation: Orthogonality is a useful tool in operator theory, and the authors aim to refine existing notions of numerical radius orthogonality by defining a stronger variant.
method: Pure operator-theoretic analysis: definition of strong numerical radius orthogonality, followed by structural properties and characterizations of both notions and their interrelation.
result: Several properties of numerical radius orthogonality and strong numerical radius orthogonality are established, along with conditions linking the two concepts.
conclusion: The new notion provides a finer classification tool for bounded linear operators, though no connection to quantum information or physics is drawn.

title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
authors: Jin-Cheng Guu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story. During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve. We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, someone must judge whether the definitions and statements express the intended mathematics and whether future updates preserve that meaning. This work, even when done, can only be trusted. We must therefore return to the usual trust model: relying on the mathematical judgment of maintainers and expert communities. But semantic review is expensive, making it tempting to keep producing code and take successful kernel checks as sufficient grounds for trust. This shortcut accumulates semantic debt: definitions and results with unchecked mathematical interpretations are reused as foundations for further work. A library may keep compiling and produce the desired formal theorem while users lose track of which mathematical claims they can responsibly rely on. Reliable reuse is also a prerequisite for Terence Tao's vision of formal mathematics as something people can navigate, explain, learn from, and build with. This paper takes our work connecting the VOA and CFSG repositories for the Moonshine Conjecture as a case study of the challenges of reliable reuse as formal developments scale.
tldr: A case-study essay on the formalization of the Moonshine Conjecture in Lean, arguing that kernel-checked proofs do not by themselves guarantee mathematical meaning or reliable reuse.
motivation: The authors want to counter the optimism that once a sufficiently large formal library compiles, the principal mathematical work is done, by highlighting two unresolved problems: whether formal statements express intended mathematics, and whether meaning survives repository evolution.
method: The paper reflects on a formalization project connecting the VOA and CFSG repositories for the Moonshine Conjecture, using it as a case study to discuss semantic review, trust models, and the accumulation of 'semantic debt'.
result: It finds that formal verification alone cannot substitute for expert mathematical judgment, and that skipping semantic review leads to definitions and results with unchecked interpretations being reused as foundations.
conclusion: Reliable formal mathematics must fall back on the trust model of maintainers and expert communities, and semantic review is essential for Terence Tao's vision of navigable, reusable formal mathematics.

title: Recursive Relations For Categorified Young Symmetrizers In Type $\mathbb{B}$
authors: Nur Cataltepe
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The category of bounded-above chain complexes of Soergel bimodules of any finite type [MATH] contains a symmetrizer complex [MATH] which kills non-identity Soergel bimodules up to homotopy. It has been shown in previous work that, in type [MATH], [MATH] can be obtained as a semi-infinite extension between copies of [MATH] and its product with a Jucys-Murphy complex. We prove an analogous recursion holds between the symmetrizers for type [MATH] and [MATH]. Following the method of the result in type [MATH], we then use this to prove that the cohomology ring of the endomorphism algebra of [MATH] is a polynomial ring.
tldr: The paper proves recursive relations for categorified Young symmetrizers in type B and uses them to show a cohomology ring is polynomial.
motivation: Categorified symmetrizers in Soergel bimodule complexes provide algebraic structures analogous to Young symmetrizers, and prior work established recursions in type A.
method: The author constructs a recursion between symmetrizers for type B and type A using semi-infinite extensions and Jucys-Murphy complexes, following the type A method.
result: An analogous recursion is established for type B, and the cohomology ring of the endomorphism algebra of the symmetrizer complex is proven to be a polynomial ring.
conclusion: The results extend the type A recursive structure to type B and identify the endomorphism cohomology as polynomial, contributing to categorified representation theory.

title: Degree-stratified Randomized Projection For Spectral Clustering
authors: Junghyun Eom, Youngjin Hwang, Euihyun Kim, Yongseok Jang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many real-world networks have heavy-tailed degree distributions, in which a few high-degree nodes coexist with many low-degree nodes. Randomized range finders reduce the cost of computing the eigenspace used in spectral clustering, but their random test matrices are constructed independently of the node degrees. We propose degree-stratified randomized projection (DS-RP), which partitions the nodes into dyadic degree strata, distributes a fixed sketch dimension across the strata, and draws an independent local sketch for each stratum. We bound the angle between the sampled range and the target eigenspace and show that the gain comes from the allocation of the sketch dimension rather than from the stratification itself. The bound improves when more sketch dimensions are assigned to the strata on which the target eigenspace is concentrated. For the degree-corrected stochastic block model, we prove that the leverage scores of this eigenspace are proportional to the node degrees, so that the allocation can be determined from the degrees alone. A Rayleigh--Ritz bound that requires no smallness assumption carries the estimate over to the computed spectral embedding. Numerical experiments on synthetic benchmarks and real-world networks show that DS-RP improves the clustering accuracy of standard Gaussian and CountSketch projections at the same sketch dimension and essentially the same computational cost.
tldr: The paper introduces degree-stratified randomized projection (DS-RP), a sketching method that allocates sketch dimensions across degree strata to speed up spectral clustering on heavy-tailed networks.
motivation: Standard randomized range finders for spectral clustering build random test matrices independently of node degrees, which is inefficient for networks with heavy-tailed degree distributions.
method: Nodes are partitioned into dyadic degree strata, a fixed sketch dimension is distributed across strata with independent local sketches, and the subspace angle is bounded; for degree-corrected stochastic block models the leverage scores are shown to be proportional to node degrees, and a Rayleigh-Ritz bound transfers the estimate to the spectral embedding.
result: The bound shows the improvement stems from sketch-dimension allocation rather than stratification, and experiments on synthetic and real networks show higher clustering accuracy than Gaussian and CountSketch projections at the same sketch dimension and comparable cost.
conclusion: Degree-aware allocation of sketching budget yields better spectral clustering on heavy-tailed graphs without extra computational cost.

title: Isomorphic Nonembeddings Of Lorentz Spaces Under Tensor Products
authors: Ying Xu, Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lorentz quasi-norm on [MATH] is \[ \|f\|_{p,q} =\left(\int_0^1 [t^{1/p}f^*(t)]^q\,{t}\right)^{1/q}, \] where [MATH] is the decreasing rearrangement of [MATH]. Motivated by the isomorphic classification of Lorentz spaces (KuryakovSukochev2015,HuangSukochev2021), we ask whether [MATH] persists under projective tensoring with a common factor. For [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], we obtain the following results. Nonzero finite-dimensional factors preserve the nonembedding, as do nonzero [MATH]-FDD factors when [MATH]. A single factor [MATH] makes both tensor products isomorphic to [MATH] throughout this range. For each pair with [MATH], there are two nonisomorphic separable absorbers with the metric approximation property. For [MATH], a scalar [MATH] factor over a standard probability space yields an embedding exactly when the nonatomic part of [MATH] has positive measure. For [MATH] and [MATH], we construct common absorbers under [MATH]-projective tensoring after equivalent renorming.
tldr: A pure functional-analysis paper studying when isomorphic nonembeddings of Lorentz spaces survive projective tensor products with common factors.
motivation: Motivated by the isomorphic classification of Lorentz spaces, the authors ask whether the nonembeddability of one Lorentz space into another persists after tensoring both with a shared factor.
method: The authors analyze projective tensor products of Lorentz spaces L_{p,q} for various parameter ranges, examining finite-dimensional factors, FDD factors, and scalar L_infinity factors over standard probability spaces.
result: They show finite-dimensional and certain FDD factors preserve nonembedding, that a single L1-type factor trivializes both tensor products to be isomorphic to L1, and construct nonisomorphic separable absorbers with the metric approximation property for each pair.
conclusion: The work extends the isomorphic classification of Lorentz spaces to tensor-product settings, characterizing when nonembedding phenomena are stable under projective tensoring and identifying common absorbers.

title: A Higher-Order Algorithm For Solving Time-Fractional Differential Equations Via Rational Approximation Of Z^{\alpha} As A Herglotz-Nevanlinna Function
authors: Miao-Jung Yvonne Ou, Gamze Tano\v{g}lu, Jiangming Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-Fractional derivatives (TFDs) have been widely used in mathematical modeling of physical phenomena such as anomalous diffusion and memory effects of materials. Traditionally, TFD is handled {either by a direct method which saves almost all the memory and hence computationally expensive or a sum of exponential method (SOE) which decomposes the time domain improper integral into a local term and a history term} {approximated by} a sum of exponential functions. The limitation of the SOE approach is that{ the approximation error of the local term might result in large errors if the unknown function is not smooth enough at [MATH] and can lead to over-dissipation of energy.} In this paper, we take a different approach and will focus on the Caputo derivative because the Caputo time derivative of a constant function is 0. We present a simple time-stepping algorithm based on the theory of Stieltjes-Markov functions, a subclass of the Herglotz-Nevanlinna functions. The key is in identifying the Stieltjes-Markov function structure hidden in the Laplace transform of the kernel function. Compared to most of the current methods in literature, the novelty of the results in this paper is manifold. First, no decomposition of integral is needed and our resulting approximation in the time domain contains a Dirac measure with carefully calculated strength, leading to a drastic decrease in the number of exponential functions needed in the approximation. Secondly, the choice of our interpolation points is based on the Mellin's inversion theorem and hence the interpolation error in the transformed domain is explicitly and rigorously linked to the error in the time-domain. {Finally, the resulting system is almost diagonal and hence can be easily sped up by using the Schur complement method.}.
tldr: The paper presents a higher-order time-stepping algorithm for Caputo time-fractional differential equations using rational approximation of z^α via Stieltjes-Markov/Herglotz-Nevanlinna functions.
motivation: Existing methods for time-fractional derivatives are either memory-intensive or rely on sum-of-exponentials approximations that can cause large errors and over-dissipation when solutions are nonsmooth.
method: The authors exploit the Stieltjes-Markov structure in the Laplace transform of the kernel, avoid integral decomposition, and construct an approximation with a Dirac measure and Mellin-inversion-based interpolation points to link transformed-domain error to time-domain error.
result: The resulting scheme requires fewer exponential functions and yields an almost diagonal system that can be accelerated with the Schur complement method.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm provides an efficient and rigorously justified numerical approach for time-fractional differential equations, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Simple Yetter-Drinfeld Modules And Extensions Over Fractional Infinite-Dimensional Taft Algebras
authors: Yiwei Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all simple Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a fractional infinite-dimensional Taft Hopf algebra [MATH], including the infinite-dimensional induced family and the finite-dimensional truncated and cyclic families. We determine their explicit structures and isomorphism criteria, and classify first extensions between finite-dimensional simple modules together with their middle modules. We also establish the primary decomposition with respect to [MATH] and prove that every nonzero-eigenvalue component is wild when [MATH].
tldr: The paper classifies simple Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a fractional infinite-dimensional Taft Hopf algebra, including induced, truncated, and cyclic families, and classifies first extensions between finite-dimensional simple modules.
motivation: Yetter-Drinfeld modules over infinite-dimensional Hopf algebras remain poorly classified, and the fractional Taft algebra provides a tractable but rich algebraic setting for doing so.
method: Pure representation-theoretic/algebraic classification: explicit construction of simple modules, isomorphism criteria, computation of extension spaces and middle modules, and a primary decomposition theorem.
result: All simple Yetter-Drinfeld modules are classified into infinite-dimensional induced and finite-dimensional truncated/cyclic families with explicit structures, and every nonzero-eigenvalue component is shown to be wild under stated conditions.
conclusion: The work gives a complete structural picture of the module category and its extensions, indicating wild representation type in generic eigenvalue components.

title: User-Irrepressible Sequences For Multiple-Packet Reception
authors: Yen-Ling Shih, Yuan-Hsun Lo, Yijin Zhang, Ying Miao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies deterministic transmission schemes based on protocol sequences for slot-synchronous multiple-packet reception (MPR) channels without feedback or synchronization of sequence phases. Each user schedules its transmissions according to a preassigned periodic binary sequence. A sequence set has the user-irrepressible property with MPR capability [MATH] ([MATH]-UI) if every user is guaranteed at least one successful transmission per period, regardless of the relative cyclic shifts. We propose a unified explicit construction based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) for arbitrary MPR capability [MATH]. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified CRT-based construction framework for [MATH]-UI sequences over this full range, without requiring conflict-avoiding codes with prescribed parameters. We establish the [MATH]-UI property through bounds on pairwise Hamming cross-correlations and show that suitably selected subsets support one additional active user without increasing the sequence length. We also derive exact average individual delay expressions over all possible cyclic shifts and extend the delay analysis to [MATH]-UI sequence sets obtained from conflict-avoiding codes.
tldr: The paper proposes CRT-based deterministic protocol sequences that guarantee user-irrepressible multiple-packet reception without feedback or phase synchronization.
motivation: Slot-synchronous multiple-packet reception channels without feedback require transmission schedules that guarantee each user successful reception despite arbitrary relative cyclic shifts.
method: The authors give a unified explicit Chinese Remainder Theorem construction for M-UI sequence sets and analyze the property via pairwise Hamming cross-correlation bounds and delay expressions.
result: The construction yields M-UI sequences for arbitrary MPR capability, supports an extra active user for suitable subsets without increasing sequence length, and provides exact average individual delay formulas.
conclusion: The work establishes a general CRT-based framework for user-irrepressible sequences in classical multiple-packet reception networks, extending delay analysis to sequences derived from conflict-avoiding codes.

title: Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator For Optimal Control Of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Under Uncertainty
authors: Fabricio Oliveira Oliver Lundqvist
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve open-loop optimal control problems under parametric uncertainty using a physics-informed DeepONet that returns trajectories for all sampled scenarios in one evaluation. Trained only on the residual at generic controls, the operator is reused across targets and horizons. Because a gradient-based optimizer exploits surrogate errors, we correct the prediction by one Newton step on the dynamics, computed for all scenarios and times by one parallel scan. The corrected state has a second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest for every control up to the sampling error. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.
tldr: A physics-informed DeepONet with a Newton-step correction solves open-loop optimal control problems for fixed-wing UAVs under parametric uncertainty, matching Adam and Ipopt accuracy while running 8-15x faster.
motivation: Optimal control under parametric uncertainty requires solving many scenario trajectories, which is expensive with standard batched solvers; a reusable operator surrogate could amortize this cost.
method: Train a physics-informed DeepONet on dynamics residuals at generic controls so the operator transfers across targets and horizons, then apply a single Newton correction step on the dynamics computed for all scenarios and times via a parallel scan.
result: The corrected state error is second-order and bounded by the residual, the corrected cost is honest for every control up to sampling error, and on a fixed-wing UAV benchmark it matches batched Adam and Ipopt accuracy while being 8x faster than Adam on GPU and 15x faster than Ipopt on CPU.
conclusion: Error-corrected physics-informed operators offer a fast, accurate surrogate approach to uncertainty-aware optimal control, though the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Data Informativity For Robust Feedback Rectification Of Switched Linear Systems
authors: Hannes Gernandt, Philipp Schmitz, Maria C. Honecker, Karl Worthmann
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feedback rectification is a method for switched linear systems that constructs a mode-dependent state feedback such that the closed-loop subsystems share a common eigenvector basis. If the assigned eigenvalues lie inside the unit disk, this yields a common quadratic Lyapunov function and guarantees exponential stability under arbitrary switching. In this paper, we study robust feedback rectification from input-state data affected by bounded disturbances. Using the concept of data informativity, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for approximate feedback rectification without requiring full row-rank of the collected input-state data. If the rectification error is smaller than the stability margin of the prescribed eigenvalues, we obtain global exponential stability under arbitrary switching in the disturbance-free case, and practical global asymptotic stability under bounded disturbances. The approach is illustrated by a mass-spring-damper chain with varying stiffness, where prescribed poles are assigned in every mode from data that do not determine the system matrices uniquely.
tldr: The paper derives necessary and sufficient data-informativity conditions for robust mode-dependent feedback rectification of switched linear systems from noisy input-state data, guaranteeing stability under arbitrary switching.
motivation: Feedback rectification typically requires knowledge of system matrices, but in practice only disturbance-affected input-state data are available, and the collected data may not have full row rank.
method: Using the concept of data informativity, the authors formulate conditions under which a common eigenvector basis and stabilizing eigenvalue assignment can be achieved from bounded-disturbance data without full-rank requirements.
result: Approximate feedback rectification is shown to be possible under necessary and sufficient data-informativity conditions; if the rectification error is below the stability margin, the closed loop is globally exponentially stable (disturbance-free) or practically globally asymptotically stable (bounded disturbances).
conclusion: The approach is demonstrated on a mass-spring-damper chain with varying stiffness, where prescribed poles are assigned per mode from data that do not uniquely determine the system matrices.

title: A Geometric Approach To The Classification Of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
authors: Jun Zhang Chenxu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] with [MATH]. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over [MATH]. Our approach begins with a characterization of [MATH]-homogeneous functions: the conditions [MATH] and [MATH] for every [MATH] and [MATH] hold if and only if the projective graph of [MATH] is a [MATH]-arc in [MATH]. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of [MATH]-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for [MATH], that [MATH] is locally-APN if and only if [MATH] for some [MATH] satisfying [MATH]. Together with the known case [MATH] and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.
tldr: The paper develops a geometric classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over finite fields using projective arcs.
motivation: Locally-APN functions are important in cryptography and finite geometry, and a complete classification of Niho-type cases was previously conjectured.
method: The authors characterize homogeneous functions via projective graphs and arcs, then apply the classification of arcs and their stabilizers to Niho-type power functions.
result: They prove a complete classification for the relevant cases, confirming the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.
conclusion: This is a purely classical finite-field/cryptography result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Karcher Means Of Structured Matrices Are Asymptotically Structured: A Study Via Schatten Estimates For The Additive Richardson Iteration
authors: Samuele Ferri, Valerio Loi, Stefano Serra-Capizzano, Giacomo Tento
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present work, we first study the additive Richardson iteration for the Karcher mean of complex Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrix sequences, by obtaining normalized Schatten estimates independent of the matrix dimension. These estimates are used to prove that Karcher means of structured matrices are asymptotically structured and this is proven for input HPD Toeplitz and generalized locally Toeplitz (GLT) matrix sequences. More precisely, we provide the a.c.s. approximation, which is the key for demonstrating the GLT closure under Schatten spectral bounds, and the GLT conclusion can be extended to matrix sequences with symbols that are positive definite almost everywhere. Ad hoc numerical experiments illustrate the spectral distribution consequences of these results and few related computational advantages. Concluding remarks and open problems are provided in the final section.
tldr: This paper studies Karcher means of Hermitian positive definite matrix sequences using additive Richardson iteration and Schatten-norm estimates, proving asymptotic structuredness for Toeplitz and GLT matrix sequences.
motivation: Karcher means on positive definite matrices are important in matrix analysis and numerical linear algebra, but their asymptotic structure for large structured matrix sequences is not fully understood.
method: The authors derive dimension-independent normalized Schatten estimates for the additive Richardson iteration applied to Karcher means of HPD matrix sequences, then use a.c.s. approximation to prove GLT closure under Schatten spectral bounds.
result: They show that Karcher means of HPD Toeplitz and generalized locally Toeplitz matrix sequences remain asymptotically structured, with numerical experiments illustrating spectral distribution consequences and computational advantages.
conclusion: The work establishes asymptotic structuredness of Karcher means for important matrix-sequence classes and provides open problems and computational implications, but it is purely numerical linear algebra with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems content.

title: Dual-Agent Drl Based Cooperative Beamforming And Trajectory Optimization For Uav-isac Networks
authors: Kaijian Yang, Feng Wang, Guojun Han, Xin Wang, Vincent K. N. Lau
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.
tldr: The paper proposes a dual-agent deep reinforcement learning scheme for joint beamforming and trajectory optimization in UAV-assisted integrated sensing and communication networks.
motivation: UAV networks providing integrated sensing and communication require managing interference, power, sensing SINR, and collision constraints across multiple base stations and UAVs.
method: The authors formulate a constrained Markov decision process and solve it with a dual-agent TD3-based MADRL scheme, where one agent learns multi-BS ISAC beamformers and another learns UAV trajectories, with closed-form receive beamformers for sensing.
result: Numerical results show improved average sum rate for communication UAVs compared with baselines while satisfying sensing SINR constraints and avoiding collisions in the evaluated settings.
conclusion: The proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme is effective for multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, but the work is classical wireless network optimization rather than quantum information research.

title: A Structured Levenberg--Marquardt Method For Binary Tensor Completion
authors: Yannan Chen, Xihong Yan, Bobin Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a structured Levenberg--Marquardt (LM) method with trust-region globalization for binary tensor completion, using triple decomposition and a logistic loss. Under a local component-residual error bound and positive outer curvature, we prove quadratic convergence of the exact iteration for damping exponents [MATH], without requiring full row rank. A constant-rank criterion and an explicit rank-one certificate provide sufficient conditions for the residual error bound. The analysis decomposes the local error into outer-loss linearization, factor linearization, and regularization contributions. For a symmetric nonquadratic logistic--LSE family with [MATH], cancellation improves the objective-model error to fourth order and the decrease-ratio error to second order. A synthetic experiment illustrates the local quadratic convergence rate. On the HCP and Enron datasets, the proposed method improves binary tensor completion accuracy while requiring fewer outer iterations than the first-order methods.
tldr: The paper develops a structured Levenberg--Marquardt method for binary tensor completion using triple decomposition and logistic loss, with local quadratic convergence analysis.
motivation: Binary tensor completion is a numerical optimization problem where efficient algorithms and convergence guarantees are desirable, especially without requiring full row rank.
method: The authors propose a trust-region-globalized structured Levenberg--Marquardt algorithm based on triple decomposition and logistic loss, and analyze its exact iteration convergence under local error-bound and curvature assumptions.
result: They prove quadratic convergence for certain damping exponents, derive a constant-rank criterion and rank-one certificate, and show improved accuracy with fewer outer iterations than first-order methods on HCP and Enron datasets.
conclusion: The method provides theoretical convergence guarantees and empirical improvements for binary tensor completion, but it is a classical numerical optimization contribution unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Non-local Ergodic Measures In Symplectic Dynamics
authors: Jaime Paradela
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one acts on a compact surface and has a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic perturbation of this system displays a large normally hyperbolic lamination on which the natural invariant measure is ergodic. The proof, which introduces a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity, combines tools ranging from KAM theory to geometric measure theory and is robust enough to be of interest in more general configurations.
tldr: The paper constructs normally hyperbolic laminations with ergodic invariant measures arising from real-analytic perturbations of products of symplectomorphisms, using KAM theory and geometric measure theory.
motivation: The authors aim to exhibit a new geometric mechanism, termed semi-local ergodicity, that produces ergodic invariant measures in symplectic dynamical systems beyond standard uniformly hyperbolic settings.
method: They consider a product of two symplectomorphisms — one with a basic set and one acting on a compact surface with a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium — and, under a local domination condition, analyze typical real-analytic perturbations via KAM theory combined with geometric measure theory.
result: Typical real-analytic perturbations are shown to possess a large normally hyperbolic lamination whose natural invariant measure is ergodic.
conclusion: The construction provides a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity and is robust enough to apply to broader configurations of symplectic dynamics.

title: Consensus Of Consensus: Decentralized Consensus-Based Optimization
authors: Stefania Bellavia, Massimo Fornasier, Greta Malaspina, Tim Roith
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a decentralized variant of Consensus-Based Optimization (CBO) for the global minimization of continuous, possibly non-convex functions accessible only through a stochastic, possibly biased, zeroth-order oracle with bounded mean-squared error. The agents are split among [MATH] units of an undirected communication network. Each unit evolves its swarm of [MATH] agents towards a local tracking variable, which follows the network average of the local consensus points through one round of neighbour-to-neighbour communication via a doubly stochastic mixing matrix, without any central coordinator. We show that, under an explicit condition linking the drift and diffusion parameters to [MATH], all agents reach consensus almost surely, at an exponential mean-square rate governed by the spectrum of the mixing matrix. Using a finite-agent quantitative Laplace principle, we prove that, for large [MATH] and provided some agent visits a neighbourhood of the global minimizer with sufficient probability, the expected mean-squared distance of the swarm from the minimizer falls below any tolerance within an explicit number of iterations, at a rate that deteriorates for poorly connected networks. We verify this hitting assumption for a simplified dynamics. Experiments on benchmarks up to dimension [MATH], with stochastic objectives, and on a federated learning task demonstrate the method's effectiveness.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes a decentralized consensus-based optimization method for global minimization of continuous non-convex functions using stochastic zeroth-order oracles over a network.
motivation: The authors aim to extend Consensus-Based Optimization to decentralized settings where agents communicate over an undirected network without a central coordinator.
method: Agents are partitioned into network units, each maintaining a swarm that tracks a local variable updated via doubly stochastic neighbor mixing; convergence is analyzed using a finite-agent quantitative Laplace principle.
result: Under explicit parameter and hitting conditions, all agents reach consensus almost surely at an exponential mean-square rate, and the expected squared distance to the global minimizer can be made arbitrarily small within a finite iteration count.
conclusion: The method is shown to be effective on high-dimensional stochastic benchmarks and a federated learning task, with performance depending on network connectivity.

title: Suffused NV-FETs For Reconfigurable Hardware
authors: Alexander J. Edwards, Son T. Le, Thomas Broadfoot, Samuel W. Lagasse, Collin R. Sanborn, Nicholas A. Blumenschein, Aubrey T. Hanbicki, Adam L. Friedman
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a new category of programmable device, the non-volatile (NV) suffused FET, in response to recent advances in photo- [1]-[3] and e-beam doping [4] We demonstrate that the writing mechanism of suffused NV FETs largely reduces the required access circuitry compared with other NV switches, and that with available configurations as a closed switch, open switch, NFET, or PFET, the suffused NV FET is ideal for configuration storage in reconfigurable arrays, reducing FET count in one case by 84.5%.
tldr: The paper introduces non-volatile suffused FETs as programmable devices for reconfigurable hardware, demonstrating reduced access circuitry and FET count.
motivation: Recent advances in photo- and e-beam doping motivate new programmable non-volatile device categories for compact configuration storage in reconfigurable arrays.
method: The authors define suffused NV-FETs and analyze their writing mechanism and possible configurations as closed/open switches or NFET/PFET devices.
result: Suffused NV-FETs reduce required access circuitry compared with other NV switches and can reduce FET count by 84.5% in one configuration-storage case.
conclusion: Suffused NV-FETs are proposed as efficient configuration-storage elements for reconfigurable hardware arrays.

title: Incentive Compatible Mechanisms For Sequential Fair Resource Allocation With Private Demands
authors: Ramtin Salamat, Sean R. Sinclair, Seyed M. R. Iravani
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a strategic variant of the canonical online fair allocation problem, where a planner must sequentially allocate a divisible resource to agents with privately known demands. At each stage, the planner announces an allocation rule, the agent reports their demand, and the planner allocates resources according to the rule and the reported demand. Unlike the standard model, we allow agents to strategically misreport their needs, as can arise in nonprofit settings where demand is self-reported and monetary transfers are unavailable. We characterize the structure of incentive-compatible (IC) allocation rules in this model, and use this to identify conditions under which the optimal mechanism has a simple cap structure. We then develop an approximation method for the optimal IC mechanism through a careful reduction of the discretized dynamic program to a longest-path problem on a directed acyclic graph. Numerical experiments show that ignoring strategic reporting can be substantially more costly than imposing incentive compatibility.
tldr: The paper studies incentive-compatible mechanisms for sequentially allocating a divisible resource among agents with privately known demands.
motivation: In nonprofit or self-reported demand settings without monetary transfers, agents may strategically misreport their needs, so the planner must design allocation rules robust to strategic behavior.
method: The authors characterize incentive-compatible allocation rules, identify conditions yielding an optimal cap structure, and reduce a discretized dynamic program to a longest-path problem on a DAG for approximation.
result: They derive structural properties of optimal IC mechanisms and show numerically that ignoring strategic reporting can be substantially costlier than enforcing incentive compatibility.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism-design framework for sequential fair allocation under private demands, with an approximation method and evidence for the importance of incentive compatibility.

title: Compiling Existential-Positive Queries To Bounded-Variable Fragments
authors: Hubie Chen Christoph Berkholz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A crucial property of bounded-variable fragments of first-order logic is that they can be evaluated in polynomial time. It is therefore a useful preprocessing step to rewrite, if possible, a first-order query to a logically equivalent one with a minimum number of variables. However, it may occur that reducing the number of variables causes an increase in formula size. We investigate this trade-off for the existential-positive fragment of first-order queries, where variable minimisation is decidable in general. In particular, we study the blow-up in the formula size when compiling existential-positive queries to the bounded variable fragment of positive first-order logic. While the increase of the formula size is always at most exponential, we identify situations (based on the signature and the number of variables) where only a polynomial blow-up is needed. In all other cases, we show that an exponential lower bound on the formula size of the compiled formula that matches the general upper bound. This exponential lower bound is unconditional, and is the first unconditional lower bound for formula size with respect to the studied compilation; it is proved via establishing a novel interface with circuit complexity which may be of future interest.
tldr: The paper studies the formula-size blow-up when compiling existential-positive first-order queries into bounded-variable fragments, establishing polynomial cases and unconditional exponential lower bounds via connections to circuit complexity.
motivation: Bounded-variable fragments of first-order logic are tractable, so rewriting queries to minimize variables is useful preprocessing, but variable reduction may increase formula size. The paper investigates this trade-off for existential-positive queries.
method: The authors analyze variable minimization for the existential-positive fragment and characterize signature- and variable-dependent cases where only polynomial blow-up occurs. For remaining cases, they prove exponential lower bounds using a novel interface with circuit complexity.
result: They show that the formula-size increase is at most exponential, identify situations requiring only polynomial blow-up, and prove matching unconditional exponential lower bounds in all other cases. This yields the first unconditional lower bound for formula size in the studied compilation.
conclusion: The work provides a sharp characterization of the variable-minimization versus formula-size trade-off for existential-positive queries and introduces a circuit-complexity connection that may be useful more broadly.

title: Privacy Protection In Self-Evolving Personal Agents: Persistent Memory And Cross-Carrier Transfer
authors: Zibin Lin, Taotao Wang, Shengli Zhang
