abstract: ArXiv:2611.26983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal agents carry private experience into later decisions through persistent memory. This thematic survey compares memory admission, maintenance, release, and withdrawal by protected change, observer, and validation setting. Direct evidence in the screened corpus comes from controlled memory workflows. Three worked scenarios follow one private fact through booking, feedback-driven learning, and withdrawal. We show when prompt revision and memory reads compose, when skills inherit a private head's bound, and why reader non-use does not establish cleanup of learned state. Diagnostic experiments measure the utility costs of wider label protection and broad memory deletion, and test how missing lineage obscures descendants.
tldr: A thematic survey of privacy protection mechanisms—memory admission, maintenance, release, and withdrawal—for self-evolving personal AI agents with persistent memory and cross-carrier transfer.
motivation: Personal agents accumulate private experience in persistent memory, creating privacy risks that are poorly characterized, especially when learned state propagates across agents or carriers.
method: The authors survey a screened corpus of controlled memory workflows, organize mechanisms by protected change, observer, and validation setting, and illustrate with three worked scenarios (booking, feedback-driven learning, withdrawal) plus diagnostic experiments on label protection and memory deletion costs.
result: Prompt revision and memory reads can compose in ways that leak private facts; skills may inherit a private head's bound; and reader non-use does not guarantee cleanup of learned state, with missing lineage obscuring descendant leakage.
conclusion: Effective privacy protection for self-evolving agents requires lineage-aware memory lifecycle management, since deletion and non-use alone do not ensure removal of learned private information.

title: "More Than You Expect!": Leakage-Abuse Attacks On Encrypted Vector Search
authors: Yang Zhang, Ruiqi He, Xiaoqian Sun, Siyi Lv, Zheli Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector databases support semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation, but embeddings, queries, and record labels may contain sensitive information. Although encrypted vector search protects these contents, some schemes expose records retrieved together across queries. We identify semantic neighborhood leakage, whereby co-retrieval relationships derived from access patterns reveal semantic categories of encrypted records and queries. We present SAGE (Semantic Access-pattern Graph Exploitation), a passive, persistent leakage-abuse attack that infers record labels and query categories from access patterns. SAGE builds a weighted co-retrieval graph and offers two variants requiring different auxiliary knowledge. SAGE-Dist matches anonymous spectral groups to semantic categories using estimated class proportions and refines labels via optimal transport, without known record labels. SAGE-Known combines graph-based label propagation with spectral-group anchor voting using a small set of known labels. We evaluate SAGE on four text and image datasets. With 1% known record labels, SAGE-Known achieves up to 84.3% mean record-label accuracy and outperforms the strongest corresponding baselines on all four datasets. With only estimated class proportions, SAGE-Dist achieves 66.9% record-label accuracy and 68.1% query-category accuracy on AG News, exceeding the strongest corresponding baselines by 21.8 and 41.9 percentage points, respectively, though performance varies across datasets. Experiments with a real-world DCPE implementation (Fuchsbauer et al., SCN'22) show that semantic leakage persists under encrypted approximate retrieval. These findings expose privacy risks even when vector contents remain protected.
tldr: SAGE is a passive leakage-abuse attack that exploits co-retrieval access patterns in encrypted vector search to infer record labels and query categories.
motivation: Encrypted vector search hides content but leaks access patterns; the authors show that semantic neighborhood leakage from co-retrieved records can reveal sensitive semantic categories.
method: The attack builds a weighted co-retrieval graph and offers two variants: SAGE-Dist, which matches spectral groups to categories via estimated class proportions and optimal transport, and SAGE-Known, which combines label propagation with spectral-group anchor voting.
result: On four text and image datasets, SAGE-Known reaches up to 84.3% record-label accuracy with 1% known labels, while SAGE-Dist achieves 66.9% label and 68.1% query-category accuracy on AG News; leakage persists in a real DCPE implementation.
conclusion: Access-pattern leakage in encrypted vector databases poses serious privacy risks even when vector contents remain cryptographically protected.

title: Detecting Word-Substitution Poisoning Of A Rag Knowledge Base With Relative Entropy And Runtime Verification
authors: Ali Yousefi, Nikos Komninos, Hafizul Asad
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system answers questions using passages it retrieves from a knowledge base, so users must trust that knowledge base. We study an attacker who quietly edits existing passages by swapping words for synonyms (PWWS, TextFooler) in a cybersecurity RAG system built from MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC. Using a reviewed 44-question benchmark, repeated paired runs and a control corpus in which only the layout changes, we find that poisoning lowers judged answer correctness from 0.714 to 0.555. The damage comes mostly from lost evidence and refusals, not from false statements. To find the edited passages, we use relative entropy. Comparing a whole passage with normal text is a weak signal. Still, one term of the relative entropy, the log-ratio between a word and its most probable synonym, works well: with a small language model as the reference, it reaches an AUROC of 0.95 and stays near chance on the control. Used as a retrieval filter, it halves how often edited text reaches the generator, and an attacker who must keep each passage as probable under the language model fails on all 57 sections it tries. Filtering does not restore correctness, because the edited passage is usually the one that held the answer. We therefore add a runtime monitor that checks each answer against trusted MITRE STIX data and remembers the passages it rejects. On its own, it reduces exposure to edited text from 0.41 to 0.26; when it may add the trusted MITRE entry as a source, correctness rises to 0.786. We report the costs and failure cases of every defence alongside its gains.
tldr: The paper detects word-substitution poisoning attacks on a retrieval-augmented generation knowledge base by exploiting a single relative-entropy log-ratio term plus a runtime verification monitor against trusted MITRE STIX data.
motivation: Users of RAG systems must trust the underlying knowledge base, so silent synonym-substitution edits by an attacker can degrade answer correctness without obvious false statements, and cheap detection mechanisms are needed.
method: The authors build a cybersecurity RAG system over MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC, poison passages with PWWS and TextFooler synonym swaps, and score passages using the log-ratio between a word and its most probable synonym under a small language model, combined with a runtime monitor checking answers against trusted STIX data.
result: Poisoning lowers judged correctness from 0.714 to 0.555; the log-ratio detector reaches AUROC 0.95 while staying near chance on a layout-only control, halves edited text reaching the generator, and the runtime monitor cuts exposure from 0.41 to 0.26, raising correctness to 0.786 when the trusted entry may be added as a source.
conclusion: Relative-entropy filtering and runtime verification mitigate but do not fully restore correctness, since the poisoned passage often holds the answer; the authors report costs and failure cases for each defence.

title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting Vlm Backdoors With Weight-Space Programming
authors: Ahaan Dabholkar, Harshvardhan Patel, Michalis Polychronakis, Saurabh Bagchi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can reason directly about the weights of other neural networks. Given only a natural-language objective, an LLM can inspect a model's weights, understand what they compute, and edit them directly without gradient-based optimization. This capability, termed weight-space programming (WSP), has been used to improve model performance on math reasoning, medical QA and other benchmarks. We propose TrojanMaxxing, a novel strategy to backdoor vision-language models (VLMs), by reframing it as a WSP task. We use Claude Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 agents to backdoor VLMs without any optimization or training methods. The agents inspect the model weights, apply targeted edits, and co-design an imperceptible visual trigger that activates the backdoor. We then study the agents' strategies and present a thorough evaluation of the trojaned models on various benchmark datasets. TrojanMaxxing achieves attack success rates of 93%-100% on content moderation and 78%-100% on OCR while maintaining clean accuracy. Perhaps most consequentially, we show that injecting backdoors in a training-free manner is possible by simply, "asking an agent to do it".
tldr: The authors introduce TrojanMaxxing, a training-free method that uses LLM agents performing weight-space programming to inject backdoors into vision-language models along with imperceptible visual triggers.
motivation: Recent work shows LLMs can inspect and directly edit the weights of other networks (weight-space programming); the authors ask whether this capability can be weaponized to backdoor VLMs without any gradient-based optimization or training.
method: Claude Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 agents inspect a VLM's weights, apply targeted edits, and co-design an imperceptible visual trigger, with the agents' strategies analyzed and the resulting trojaned models benchmarked.
result: Attack success rates reach 93%-100% on content moderation and 78%-100% on OCR while clean accuracy is maintained.
conclusion: Backdoors can be injected into VLMs in a training-free manner simply by asking an autonomous agent to do it, raising significant AI security concerns.

title: The Complexity Of Fair And Stable Data Exchange
authors: Bhaskar Ray Chaudhury Hannaneh Akrami
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data exchange is a fundamental challenge for Web applications such as recommender systems, personalized search, and fraud detection, where combining data across participants can improve predictions. Sustaining such collaboration requires fair returns for contributions and protection against groups leaving for a more beneficial exchange. These requirements are captured by reciprocity, which equates each participant's received utility with its credited contribution to others, and core stability, which rules out any coalition exchanging its own data to make every member strictly better off. Akrami et al. prove that such exchanges exist under broad assumptions, but leave efficient computation open. Two fundamental cases are submodular utilities, capturing diminishing returns from overlapping datasets, and supermodular utilities, capturing complementarities. We settle the approximate computation of reciprocal and core-stable exchanges in both cases, establishing a computational separation under Shapley sharing. For cross-monotone shares, which include Shapley shares under monotone submodular utilities, we give a circulation algorithm that computes an exactly core-stable, [MATH]-reciprocal exchange in time poly[MATH] given efficient access to approximate shares, where [MATH] is the number of participants and [MATH] bounds how fast each donor's credit changes with its own contribution. This yields an FPTAS when [MATH] is polynomially bounded. In contrast, finding an [MATH]-reciprocal, [MATH]-core-stable exchange is PPAD-hard for monotone lattice-supermodular utilities, even at inverse-polynomial accuracy, with constant [MATH] and exact polynomial-time evaluation of Shapley shares. Thus overlapping information permits efficient fair and stable exchange, while complementarities create a computational barrier even when contribution credits are easy to evaluate.
tldr: The paper settles the computational complexity of computing approximately reciprocal and core-stable data exchanges for submodular and supermodular utilities, giving a circulation-based FPTAS under cross-monotone/Shapley sharing and a PPAD-hardness result for lattice-supermodular utilities.
motivation: Data exchange among web applications requires fair compensation and stability against coalition defection, properties formalized as reciprocity and core stability; existence was known but efficient computation was open.
method: A polynomial-time circulation algorithm computing exactly core-stable, approximately reciprocal exchanges for cross-monotone shares (including Shapley shares under monotone submodular utilities), complemented by a PPAD-hardness reduction for monotone lattice-supermodular utilities with exactly evaluable Shapley shares.
result: Overlapping (submodular) information admits efficient fair and stable exchange yielding an FPTAS, whereas complementarities (supermodular utilities) make even inverse-polynomial approximation PPAD-hard, establishing a computational separation.
conclusion: The work delineates a sharp computational boundary between submodular and supermodular data-exchange settings, showing that complementarities constitute a fundamental barrier to fair, stable exchange.

title: 3d-nand-cim: A Hybrid-Bonded 3D-NAND-Flash-based Analog In-Memory-Compute Macro Offering 4.8m Weights/mm$^2$
authors: Pritish Narayanan, Athanasios Vasilopoulos, Geoffrey W. Burr, Manuel Le Gallo, Bill Filipiak, Hernan Castro, Jeremy Binfet, Jeremy Hirst, Henry Utomo, Kunal Parekh, Bharat Bhushan, Rajasekhar Venigalla, Kyle Kirby, Urs Egger, Jose Luquin, Vara Prasad Jonnalagadda, Athanasios Siampakos, Theodore Antonakopoulos, Kohji Hosokawa, Masatoshi Ishii, Yasuteru Kohda, Seiji Munetoh, Abhairaj Singh, Alexander Friz, Julian B\"uchel, Iason Chalas, Charles Mackin, Akul Malhotra, Akira Goda, Duane Mills, Gregory Atwood, Mark Helm, Jeffrey Burns, Vijay Narayanan, Hsinyu Tsai, Abu Sebastian
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe an analog-in-memory-compute macro hybrid-bonding a 14nm logic die onto a 3D NAND Flash memory wafer, achieving weight density of 4.8M weights/mm[MATH]. Weights are programmed to 1-of-16 conductances. MACs with current-controlled oscillator ADCs show weight-equivalent precision between 3 and 4 bits for 8-bit inputs on multiple NAND tiers at energy efficiencies up to 4.2 TOPS/W. A charge-retention circuit improves accuracy, with [MATH]0.4% (3.23%) accuracy drop on a WideResNet for CIFAR-10 (100).
tldr: The paper presents a hybrid-bonded 3D-NAND-flash analog in-memory-compute macro for neural network inference with high weight density and energy efficiency.
motivation: Analog in-memory computing can improve energy efficiency and density for AI workloads by performing MAC operations directly in memory arrays.
method: A 14nm logic die is hybrid-bonded onto a 3D NAND Flash wafer, with weights programmed as 1-of-16 conductance levels and current-controlled oscillator ADCs used for MAC readout.
result: The macro achieves 4.8M weights/mm^2, 3-4 bits weight-equivalent precision for 8-bit inputs, up to 4.2 TOPS/W, and small accuracy drops on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with a charge-retention circuit.
conclusion: Hybrid-bonded 3D NAND Flash is a promising platform for dense, energy-efficient analog in-memory compute, but the work is classical hardware and not aligned with quantum information research.

title: Pushdown Reachability Requires $n^{3/2}$ Time On Multitape Turing Machines
authors: Rupak Majumdar A. R. Balasubramanian
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pushdown reachability, or equivalently, language non-emptiness of pushdown automata (PDA), is a fundamental problem in automata theory and program analysis. We show that, for every [MATH], no deterministic multitape Turing machine can decide pushdown reachability in [MATH] time, where [MATH] is the input size. The lower bound already holds for , i.e., instances in which the number of transitions is linear in the number of states. This gives the first unconditional super-linear lower bound for pushdown reachability. Furthermore, we also extend this result and show that for any [MATH] and [MATH], no deterministic multitape Turing machine can decide the intersection non-emptiness problem of one PDA and [MATH] NFAs in time [MATH], where [MATH] is the input size. Finally, pushdown reachability is well-known to be quasi-linear time equivalent to many different problems in program analysis. Our result translates to all of those problems as well and provides the first unconditional super-linear lower bounds for those problems on multitape Turing machines.
tldr: The paper proves the first unconditional super-linear lower bound for pushdown reachability, showing deterministic multitape Turing machines require n^{3/2} time.
motivation: Pushdown reachability is a fundamental automata-theory and program-analysis problem, and unconditional super-linear lower bounds for it were previously unknown.
method: The authors use Turing machine lower-bound techniques to establish time-hierarchy-style separations for pushdown reachability and extend them to intersection non-emptiness of one PDA with multiple NFAs.
result: They prove that no deterministic multitape Turing machine can decide pushdown reachability in o(n^{3/2}) time, with the bound already holding for instances where transitions are linear in states.
conclusion: The lower bound transfers to many quasi-linear-time-equivalent program-analysis problems, yielding the first unconditional super-linear lower bounds for those problems on multitape Turing machines.

title: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: How LLMs Implant Selective Backdoors Into Language Models
authors: Xuyang Liu, Zhiwei Xu, Zirui Li, Jiabao Gao, Xiaolin Peng, Weixian Deng, Tian Qiu, Hai Wan, Xibin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural network weights are usually treated as opaque artifacts of gradient descent. Recent work on weight space programming, however, suggests that large language models can inspect and rewrite another network's parameters directly. In this paper, we ask whether a general language model can turn a natural language backdoor specification into persistent, selective weight edits on its own, without gradient training, layer hints, external corpora, or a prescribed editing formula. Using DeepSeek Flash at low reasoning effort inside a restricted workspace that blocks local CPU simulation, we test three open models (Qwen3.5-0.8B, Llama-3.2-1B, SmolLM3-3B) across two review domains (IMDb and Yelp; 18 independent sessions). Evaluated in fresh processes with the editor removed, the modified checkpoints reach 99.2% mean attack success on the editing domain and 97.6% transfer success on the unseen domain, while preserving clean accuracy, low control drift, and general capabilities within 1.7 points of the base models. Our traces show that the model converges on edits in the final layer in 17 of 18 runs and discovers both dense rank-one orthogonalization and single neuron weight surgery at an average cost of \$1.74 per run.
tldr: A general-purpose LLM autonomously rewrites the weights of small open language models to implant selective backdoors specified in natural language, without gradient training or layer hints.
motivation: Weight-space programming suggests LLMs may inspect and edit other networks' parameters directly; the authors ask whether this capability can be turned into an autonomous, specification-driven backdoor injection procedure.
method: DeepSeek Flash at low reasoning effort operates in a restricted workspace (no local CPU simulation) and edits three open models (Qwen3.5-0.8B, Llama-3.2-1B, SmolLM3-3B) across IMDb and Yelp domains in 18 independent sessions, with checkpoints evaluated in fresh processes after the editor is removed.
result: Edited checkpoints achieve 99.2% mean attack success on the editing domain and 97.6% transfer to an unseen domain, while clean accuracy and general capabilities stay within 1.7 points of baselines; edits concentrate in the final layer in 17/18 runs at ~$1.74 per run.
conclusion: LLMs can autonomously perform selective, persistent weight surgery for backdoor implantation, raising clear safety and security concerns for model distribution and auditing.

title: No Polynomial-Time Algorithm For Tarski Fixed Points Unless Cryptographic Assumptions Fail
authors: Eleni Batziou, John Fearnley, Alexandros Hollender, Rahul Savani
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the time complexity of finding a Tarski fixed point. We provide a subexponential-time reduction from the Unique End of Potential Line (UEOPL) problem to the problem of finding a Tarski fixed point. Using a range of known cryptographic lower bounds for UEOPL, our reduction implies a range of conditional lower bounds on the running time of any algorithm that finds a Tarski fixed point. The strongest of these give quasi-polynomial-time lower bounds for the problem. We also obtain a similar quasi-polynomial-time lower bound for Tarski based instead on a weak exponential-time type hypothesis for UEOPL. These running time lower bounds match the recently discovered quasi-polynomial query lower bounds for the problem.
tldr: The paper proves conditional quasi-polynomial-time lower bounds for finding Tarski fixed points via a reduction from UEOPL and cryptographic assumptions.
motivation: Tarski fixed points are central in algorithmic game theory and lattice theory, and the work aims to establish the computational hardness of finding them.
method: The authors give a subexponential-time reduction from Unique End of Potential Line (UEOPL) to the Tarski fixed point problem, then combine it with known cryptographic lower bounds for UEOPL.
result: They obtain quasi-polynomial-time conditional lower bounds for Tarski fixed point algorithms, matching recent quasi-polynomial query lower bounds; similar bounds follow from a weak exponential-time hypothesis for UEOPL.
conclusion: Finding Tarski fixed points is unlikely to admit polynomial-time algorithms unless certain cryptographic assumptions fail or UEOPL has faster algorithms.

title: Thurston Measure Is Stationary With Exponential Teichm\"uller Moment
authors: Kasra Rafi Alex Eskin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1967, Furstenberg proved that every lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center admits a probability measure whose stationary measure on the associated Furstenberg boundary belongs to the Lebesgue measure class. We prove an analogue of this theorem for the action of the mapping class group on Teichm\"uller space. Every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class on the space of projective measured foliations is the stationary measure of a non-elementary random walk with a finite exponential moment in the Teichm\"uller metric.
tldr: The paper proves an analogue of Furstenberg's theorem for the mapping class group action on Teichmüller space, showing that every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class is stationary for a non-elementary random walk with finite exponential moment in the Teichmüller metric.
motivation: Furstenberg established existence of stationary measures in the Lebesgue class for lattices in semisimple Lie groups; this work seeks a corresponding result for the mapping class group and Thurston boundary.
method: The authors construct non-elementary random walks on the mapping class group with finite exponential moment in the Teichmüller metric and analyze their stationary measures on projective measured foliations.
result: Every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class is realized as the stationary measure of such a random walk.
conclusion: This provides a mapping-class-group/Teichmüller-space analogue of Furstenberg's boundary stationarity theorem, contributing to ergodic theory and geometric group theory rather than quantum information.

title: Local Connectivity Of Julia Sets Of Newton Maps Of Trigonometric And Hyperbolic Functions
authors: Sayantan Chakraborty Molla Basir Ahamed
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Newton maps of [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map [MATH], the half-planes [MATH] are repelling petals at infinity for every [MATH]. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Bara\'nski, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpi\'nska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of [MATH]. We also show that the Newton map of [MATH], where [MATH], is affinely conjugate to the sine Newton map [MATH]. The published local-connectivity theorem for [MATH] therefore applies to this entire family, including the cosine and the two hyperbolic Newton maps. We describe the invariant lines and basin geometry of the four maps and illustrate the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.
tldr: The paper studies local connectivity of Julia sets and basin boundaries for Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.
motivation: The authors aim to extend local-connectivity results for transcendental Newton maps to cosine, sine, and related hyperbolic functions with infinitely many unbounded attracting basins.
method: They explicitly identify repelling petals at infinity for the cosine Newton map and apply the tame-basin criterion of Barański, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpińska; they also use affine conjugacy to relate hyperbolic Newton maps to the sine Newton map.
result: They establish local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin for the cosine Newton map and extend the published local-connectivity theorem to the entire family via conjugacy, while describing invariant lines and basin geometry.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous complex-dynamical results on local connectivity for a class of transcendental Newton maps and illustrates the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.

title: Pathwise Factorization And Uncertainty Quantification For Impedance Obstacles With Random Boundaries
authors: Koung Hee Leem George Pelekanos
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a factorization method with finite-sample statistical guarantees for two-dimensional acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles whose boundary is random and whose data are finitely many noisy multistatic measurements. In the two-dimensional far-field normalization, the symmetrization must act on a phase-rotated far-field operator; we prove the optical and range identities for every realization of a compact family of uniformly bi-Lipschitz domains, with jointly measurable regularized indicators. A quadrature-weighted finite-sample analysis separates angular approximation, measurement noise, test-vector error, and regularization, and yields a consistency theorem for empirical means and variances, joint in all data parameters. Bounded indicators admit simultaneous confidence bands, a diagonal threshold recovers the probability that a sampling point lies in the random obstacle, and a nested design yields unbiased variance components. Computations use a combined-field integral equation proved invertible at all frequencies, and the finite-grid guarantees are examined in a coverage study against a high-accuracy Monte Carlo reference.
tldr: The paper develops a pathwise factorization method with finite-sample statistical guarantees for acoustic scattering from impedance obstacles whose boundaries are random and observed through finitely many noisy multistatic measurements.
motivation: Inverse scattering with uncertain geometry and limited noisy data requires methods that give rigorous statistical guarantees rather than only deterministic reconstructions, particularly when obstacle boundaries are random.
method: The authors prove optical and range identities for a phase-rotated far-field operator over a compact family of uniformly bi-Lipschitz domains, and combine a combined-field integral equation with a quadrature-weighted finite-sample analysis that separates angular approximation, noise, test-vector error, and regularization.
result: They obtain a consistency theorem for empirical means and variances, simultaneous confidence bands for bounded indicators, a threshold rule recovering the probability that a sampling point lies inside the random obstacle, and unbiased variance components from a nested design, validated by a coverage study against Monte Carlo reference.
conclusion: The framework yields rigorous uncertainty quantification for sampling-based obstacle reconstruction under random boundaries and noisy finite measurements, though it lies entirely in classical acoustic inverse problems.

title: AI-Assisted Decision Support For Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning And Mathematical Programming
authors: Charles Thraves Felipe M\'endez
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, in which strategists decide at each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to fit. We develop a data-driven simulator, calibrated with historical race data, that captures tire degradation, drivers' recent performance, overtaking, yellow flag events, and rivals' pit-stop decisions. We train agents with five Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms and compare them with a Quadratic Mixed-Integer Programming (QMIP) formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings. Without uncertainty or competition, all DRL methods except TRPO achieve near-optimal performance. With a full grid of competitors and stochastic race events, the ranking of DRL methods depends on the evaluation setting: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and its recurrent variant are the only methods that improve on the QMIP both in fully simulated races and when the actual 2024 races are replayed. Averaged over eight circuits, PPO improves on the QMIP by 0.33 and 0.49 positions in the two settings and Recurrent PPO by less, and in the replay PPO finishes 0.66 positions ahead of the drivers' actual strategies simulated in the same races. The QMIP performs similarly to the other methods, even though it cannot anticipate yellow flag events. Finally, we use the trained PPO policy as a look-ahead decision-support tool that shows the strategist the distribution of race outcomes under each candidate pit-stop action. Applied retrospectively to eight 2024 races, the look-ahead identifies the laps where the actual decision, the recommendation, or a third action was preferable.
tldr: The paper applies deep reinforcement learning and mixed-integer quadratic programming to optimize Formula 1 pit-stop and tire-compound decisions.
motivation: Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, where teams must decide each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to use, and better data-driven tools could support strategists.
method: The authors build a race simulator calibrated on historical data (tire degradation, driver form, overtaking, yellow flags, rival pit decisions), train agents with five DRL algorithms, and benchmark them against a QMIP formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings.
result: Without uncertainty all DRL methods except TRPO approach optimality; with a full grid and stochastic events, PPO and Recurrent PPO are the only methods that beat the QMIP, improving by 0.33 and 0.49 positions on average over eight circuits and finishing 0.66 positions ahead of actual drivers' simulated strategies in 2024 race replays.
conclusion: The trained PPO policy can serve as a look-ahead decision-support tool that shows outcome distributions for candidate pit actions, and retrospectively it identifies laps where the actual, recommended, or a third action would have been preferable.

title: When Speed Changes Where To Build: Optimal Placement Of An Optional Fast Connection
authors: Xiaofeng Nie Heng Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Express roads, limited-stop transit, and air taxis speed up only the trips that choose them, while others stay on the ground network. Where should such a connection's terminals go? Because its users change with the design, expected travel time is nonconvex and nonsmooth in the terminal locations. Previous models have therefore been solved numerically or in restricted settings. We solve a canonical case exactly: uniform trips in a square with grid streets and a straight link. We find that every optimal design is centered and diagonal or axis aligned, and the alignment switches once, near 2.18 times ground speed. The two designs tied there differ sharply in coverage and ridership. A planner also choosing speed, at a smooth cost of speed, never selects the switching speed. If the cost is proportional to speed, above a threshold unit cost the planner builds a slower diagonal link, below it a faster axis-aligned one, and the optimal speed skips a band around the switch. On a rectangle, every optimum is again centered, centered designs have a closed-form travel time, and only two families of links can be optimal, those along the long axis and those tilted toward the long side.
tldr: This paper solves exactly where to place the terminals of an optional fast connection (express road, limited-stop transit, air taxi) in a square city with grid streets, characterizing optimal designs as centered and either diagonal or axis aligned.
motivation: Because ridership depends on the design itself, expected travel time is nonconvex and nonsmooth in terminal locations, so prior work resorted to numerics or restricted settings; the authors seek a canonical closed-form case.
method: Analytical optimization of expected travel time for uniform trip demand in a square (and later rectangular) domain with grid ground travel plus a straight high-speed link, including joint optimization over link speed with smooth and proportional speed costs.
result: All optima are centered, with alignment switching once near 2.18 times ground speed where two designs tie but differ sharply in coverage and ridership; with speed choice the switching speed is never selected, and on rectangles only links along the long axis or tilted toward the long side can be optimal.
conclusion: The results give exact, interpretable guidance for planners siting fast connections and show that the speed–geometry trade-off produces discontinuous design choices and skipped speed bands.

title: A Fast Automatically Adaptive Integral Equation Solver For Nonlinear Two-point Boundary Value Systems
authors: Tianze Zhang, Yixuan Ma, Jun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a fast, high-order, automatically adaptive integral-equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems. The method builds on the fast direct solver for linear second-kind integral equations and completes the mathematical formulation needed for general boundary conditions, including cases in which the simplest background Green's function is singular and cases with genuinely rank-deficient boundary conditions. Nonlinear problems are written as nonlinear second-kind integral equations and are solved by combining this fast adaptive linear solver with Newton iteration and user-specified continuation. In this way the nonlinear solver inherits the full strengths of the linear integral-equation method: a fast direct solver, arbitrary order accuracy, and automatic adaptive resolution with only a small overhead over a solve on the final mesh. The resulting algorithm is particularly effective for problems with localized or multiscale structure, including boundary layers, dense oscillations, transition regions, hypersensitive optimal-control systems, and singular perturbations. The same framework also provides a computational foundation for future studies of bifurcation and solution-branch exploration.
tldr: A fast, high-order, automatically adaptive integral-equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems built on a fast direct linear solver combined with Newton iteration.
motivation: Nonlinear two-point boundary value problems with localized, multiscale, or singularly perturbed structure (boundary layers, dense oscillations, hypersensitive optimal control) are hard to resolve efficiently with standard numerical schemes.
method: The nonlinear problem is recast as a nonlinear second-kind integral equation; the authors complete the formulation for general boundary conditions (including singular background Green's functions and rank-deficient conditions) and solve it with a fast adaptive direct linear solver coupled to Newton iteration and user-specified continuation.
result: The nonlinear solver inherits arbitrary-order accuracy, fast direct solving, and automatic adaptive mesh resolution with only small overhead over a solve on the final mesh, proving effective on boundary layers, oscillations, transition regions, and singular perturbations.
conclusion: The framework offers an efficient general-purpose numerical tool and a foundation for future bifurcation and solution-branch exploration studies.

title: Railroads As Cyber-Physical Systems: Cybersecurity Implications Of Increasing Automation -- Threats, Consequences, And Operational Resilience
authors: Syed Owais Athar, Mohsin Kamal, Aemal Khattak, Muhammad Naveed Aman
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objectives: Rail automation improves train protection, traffic management, inspection, and operational efficiency but increases dependence on software, communications, remote access, and external providers. This paper examines its impact on railroad cyber-physical system security and operational resilience. Methods: A narrative review synthesizes railroad automation literature, OT security guidance, FRA and TSA materials, and documented rail cyber incidents. Automation functions are mapped to exposed assets, attack vectors, and operational consequences, focusing on signalling, communications, onboard systems, remote access, and human oversight. Findings: Automation shifts rail risks from isolated mechanical failures toward interconnected cyber-physical dependencies. Key vulnerabilities involve train detection, positioning, signalling, grade crossings, remote diagnostics, vendor access, and AI-enabled monitoring. Cyber incidents can cause operational disruption, supply-chain impacts, and national-security risks, even when fail-safe mechanisms prevent catastrophic outcomes. Novelty: The paper introduces a rail-specific taxonomy connecting automation functions, cyberattack pathways, operational consequences, and resilience requirements, framing cybersecurity as an operational rather than purely IT concern. Practical Applications: The framework supports security-by-design procurement, IT/OT segmentation, secure remote access and software updates, degraded-mode planning, trusted recovery, and human oversight. Operators and regulators can use it to assess automation deployments and mitigate cyber risks.
tldr: A narrative review mapping railroad automation functions to cyber-physical vulnerabilities, attack pathways, operational consequences, and resilience requirements.
motivation: Rail automation increases dependence on software, communications, remote access, and third-party vendors, shifting risk from isolated mechanical failures toward interconnected cyber-physical dependencies that are poorly captured by traditional IT-centric security framings.
method: Narrative literature synthesis of railroad automation research, OT security guidance, FRA/TSA materials, and documented rail cyber incidents; automation functions are mapped onto exposed assets, attack vectors, and operational consequences across signalling, communications, onboard systems, remote access, and human oversight.
result: Key vulnerabilities are identified in train detection, positioning, signalling, grade crossings, remote diagnostics, vendor access, and AI-enabled monitoring; incidents can produce operational disruption, supply-chain impacts, and national-security risk even when fail-safe mechanisms avert catastrophe.
conclusion: The paper proposes a rail-specific taxonomy framing cybersecurity as an operational rather than purely IT concern, supporting security-by-design procurement, IT/OT segmentation, secure remote access, degraded-mode planning, trusted recovery, and human oversight.

title: Manipulation-resistant Reputation For Peer-to-peer Scientific Publishing: A Combination-therapy Approach
authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Prost
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In open peer-to-peer networks, where publishing is nearly free and identities are cheap, reputation systems decide what deserves attention, and their metrics become targets for manipulation. We study how to choose and combine reputation signals so that manipulation does not pay while genuine contribution does. Inspired by combination therapies in medicine, we describe each gaming action by its effects on all signals. For aggregation by the minimum of the signals, we prove that, in a global linear model, either some mix of gaming actions raises every signal by more than it costs, or the net gain of gaming is bounded by the imbalance of the attacker's honest profile; locally, gaming brings no first-order gain exactly when an admissible weighting is supported on the attacker's weakest signals. We then specify, without implementing it, MagMell, a two-tier system for peer-to-peer scientific publication: a protocol that orders signed events by Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, enforces budgets and settles staked assessments, and open reputation algorithms that any node can run. Simulations on synthetic data show that minimum aggregation makes networks of fake identities, collusion rings and floods of generated papers lose rank beyond small intensities, at the price of a lower correlation between rank and quality for honest accounts. They also show that criticism is rarely settled, because the evidence needed is seldom available. The replicated log should grow by about 26 kilobytes per identity and year (analytic estimate), and a full recomputation of reputations takes 1.0 to 1.6 seconds for 100,000 identities (measured).
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes manipulation-resistant reputation aggregation (minimum-of-signals) for a Byzantine-fault-tolerant peer-to-peer scientific publishing system called MagMell, supported by simulations and resource estimates.
motivation: In open peer-to-peer publishing, cheap identities and near-free publication make reputation metrics targets for gaming, so the authors ask how to choose and combine reputation signals such that manipulation does not pay while genuine contribution does.
method: Each gaming action is modeled by its effect on all reputation signals, inspired by combination therapy; the authors prove results for min-aggregation in a global linear model and locally via admissible weightings, then specify a two-tier architecture (BFT-ordered signed events, staked assessments, open reputation algorithms) and evaluate it with synthetic-data simulations.
result: Minimum aggregation degrades the rank of fake-identity networks, collusion rings, and paper floods beyond small intensities, at the cost of weaker rank-quality correlation for honest accounts; criticism is rarely settled for lack of evidence, and costs are ~26 kB per identity-year with full recomputation of 100,000 identities taking 1.0-1.6 s.
conclusion: Min-aggregation of reputation signals offers a principled, manipulation-resistant design for decentralized scientific publishing, though with trade-offs in honest-user ranking and dispute resolution.

title: A Functional Breuer-Major Theorem Under Finite Variance, With Application To The $r/s$ Test For Long Memory
authors: Samir Ben Hariz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Breuer-Major theorem (Breuer and Major, 1983) states that, for a function [MATH] of Hermite rank [MATH] such that [MATH], and a stationary Gaussian sequence whose correlation function [MATH] satisfies [MATH], the finite dimensional distributions of the normalized partial sum process of [MATH] converge to those of a Brownian motion. Whether the functional version of this result holds under these sole conditions has remained open for a long time, the tightness being known only under additional moment assumptions. In this paper we prove that the functional central limit theorem holds under finite variance only. More generally, we give a high order expansion of the partial sum process which covers both short and long-range dependence: the long-range dependent components converge to Hermite processes, while the remainder converges to a Brownian motion. As an application, we discuss the question of testing long-memory in observed data using the [MATH] statistics. We derive the limiting distributions of the classical and modified [MATH] statistics, prove the consistency of the test and propose a data-driven choice of the truncation parameter. A Monte Carlo study compares the performances of the classical and modified [MATH] statistics for both short-memory and long-memory sequences.
tldr: The paper proves a functional Breuer-Major central limit theorem under only finite variance and applies it to long-memory testing via r/s statistics.
motivation: The functional version of the Breuer-Major theorem had remained open under the sole conditions of finite variance and summability of correlations, with tightness previously requiring extra moment assumptions.
method: The author establishes a high-order expansion of normalized partial sum processes for functions of stationary Gaussian sequences, separating Hermite-process long-range components from a Brownian remainder, and derives limiting distributions for classical and modified r/s statistics.
result: The functional central limit theorem holds under finite variance alone, long-range dependent components converge to Hermite processes, the remainder converges to Brownian motion, and the long-memory test is shown consistent with a data-driven truncation parameter.
conclusion: The work resolves a long-standing tightness issue in the Breuer-Major framework and provides theoretical and practical tools for long-memory testing, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Linearly Decoupled Structure-preserving Bcfd Method For The Two-species Keller--Segel Chemotaxis System
authors: Ao Zhang, Bingyin Zhang, Hongfei Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a fully discrete, linearly decoupled block-centered finite difference scheme for the two-species Keller--Segel chemotaxis system. Based on the Slotboom transformation, the cell-density equations are reformulated into a symmetric form, providing a natural framework for the construction of a structure-preserving discretization. The resulting scheme is shown to unconditionally preserve the positivity of both the cell densities and the chemoattractant concentration, while ensuring exact mass conservation of each cell density and the original energy dissipation. Furthermore, optimal-order error estimates for the proposed scheme are rigorously established through a higher-order consistency analysis. In particular, the cell densities exhibit first-order temporal and second-order spatial convergence in the discrete [MATH]-norm, whereas the chemoattractant concentration achieves the same convergence orders in the discrete [MATH]-norm. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted to verify the theoretical results and demonstrate the reliability of the proposed scheme in simulating the finite-time blow-up phenomenon.
tldr: The paper develops a linearly decoupled, structure-preserving block-centered finite difference scheme for the two-species Keller-Segel chemotaxis system.
motivation: The authors aim to construct a fully discrete numerical method that preserves key physical properties such as positivity, mass conservation, and energy dissipation for chemotaxis models.
method: Using the Slotboom transformation, the cell-density equations are reformulated into a symmetric form, and a linearly decoupled block-centered finite difference scheme is proposed with rigorous error estimates.
result: The scheme unconditionally preserves positivity and exact mass conservation while dissipating energy, and optimal-order convergence is established and verified numerically, including simulations of finite-time blow-up.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a reliable structure-preserving numerical tool for simulating two-species chemotaxis systems, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Carleman Estimates And $\phi$-null Controllability For A Fully Discrete Fourth-order Parabolic Equation
authors: P\'ia Bizama, V\'ictor Hern\'andez-Santamar\'ia, Ariel A. P\'erez, Jose Solarte
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a fully discrete approximation of a one-dimensional fourth-order parabolic equation with clamped boundary conditions, obtained by centered finite differences in space and the implicit Euler method in time, and controlled by two boundary controls acting at the left endpoint. We prove a Carleman estimate for the corresponding discrete adjoint operator, in which the large Carleman parameter is connected to the space and time discretization parameters [MATH] and [MATH]. As a consequence, we obtain a relaxed observability inequality and a [MATH]-null controllability result, in which the controls are bounded uniformly with respect to [MATH] and [MATH], and the norm of the solution at the final time is of order [MATH], with [MATH] exponentially small, provided [MATH] for some [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves Carleman estimates and phi-null controllability for a fully discrete fourth-order parabolic equation with boundary controls.
motivation: The authors aim to establish controllability properties for a discrete numerical approximation of a fourth-order parabolic PDE, with uniform control bounds independent of discretization parameters.
method: They use centered finite differences in space and the implicit Euler method in time, derive a discrete Carleman estimate for the adjoint operator, and obtain a relaxed observability inequality.
result: They prove phi-null controllability with controls bounded uniformly in space and time discretization parameters and final-time norm exponentially small under a parameter condition.
conclusion: The work provides discrete Carleman estimates and controllability results relevant to numerical analysis and PDE control theory.

title: Real-analytic Actions Of Lattices In $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ On Compact $n$-manifolds
authors: Zhiren Wang Federico Rodriguez Hertz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify real-analytic actions of arbitrary lattices in [MATH] on compact connected [MATH]-manifolds without boundary, [MATH], with no invariant-volume assumption. After finite-index restriction, the action has finite image, extends to a connected Lie group locally isomorphic to [MATH] with an equivariant finite cover when needed, or is obtained by analytic surgery with at least one torus piece. In the last case the lattice is commensurable with a conjugate of [MATH]. As a main input, we prove a general cocycle superrigidity theorem for real analytic germs.
tldr: The authors classify real-analytic actions of arbitrary lattices in SL(n,R) on compact connected n-manifolds without boundary, without any invariant-volume assumption.
motivation: Understanding which Lie group actions lattices can admit on compact manifolds is a basic rigidity question that previously required invariant-volume hypotheses; the authors aim to remove that assumption.
method: The classification proceeds via a general cocycle superrigidity theorem for real-analytic germs, combined with analytic surgery arguments producing torus pieces.
result: After passing to a finite-index subgroup, the action either has finite image, extends to a connected Lie group locally isomorphic to SL(n,R) (up to finite equivariant cover), or arises from analytic surgery with a torus piece, in which case the lattice is commensurable to a conjugate of SL(n,Z).
conclusion: The work gives a complete dichotomy for real-analytic lattice actions on compact n-manifolds and establishes a new superrigidity tool for real-analytic cocycles.

title: The Distortion Problem And Orthogonality
authors: Qi Liu Zhiyao Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schlumprecht [Israel J. Math. 76 (1991), 81--95] constructed an arbitrarily distortable Banach space. We further study distortion on this space under orthogonality constraints and obtain the following results. The exact distortion of his renormings is preserved in every infinite-dimensional subspace when the unit vectors satisfy both mutual Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality for any finite family of equivalent norms. There are basic sequences of unit vectors satisfying both orthogonality conditions pairwise whose norms in the renormed space converge to the lower distortion endpoint. The proof combines finite-dimensional norm estimates with supporting functionals and the Borsuk--Ulam theorem. Further results concern finite and approximate Roberts conditions and an obstruction to simultaneous Pythagorean orthogonality for auxiliary norms.
tldr: This pure mathematics paper studies distortion properties of Schlumprecht's arbitrarily distortable Banach space under Birkhoff–James and isosceles orthogonality constraints.
motivation: The work extends the study of distortion in Banach spaces by imposing orthogonality conditions on unit vectors, motivated by classical functional analysis and geometry of Banach spaces.
method: The authors combine finite-dimensional norm estimates, supporting functionals, and the Borsuk–Ulam theorem to analyze renormings of Schlumprecht space under orthogonality constraints.
result: They show that exact distortion is preserved in every infinite-dimensional subspace when unit vectors satisfy both orthogonality conditions for finite families of equivalent norms, and construct basic sequences whose norms converge to the lower distortion endpoint.
conclusion: The paper provides new structural results on distortability and orthogonality in Banach spaces, including finite and approximate Roberts conditions and an obstruction to simultaneous Pythagorean orthogonality.

title: Dynamic Preference Logic Of Preference Lifting
authors: Xiaochen Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In preference logic, preference is modeled as a binary relation between possible worlds. When we discuss preference relations between propositions, we also need to consider how to lift this relation between possible worlds to propositions. Here, propositions are usually represented by their extensions, that is, sets of possible worlds. There are several choices of lifting scheme: for example, one may require even the worst world in one set to be better than the best world in another, or merely require that every world in one set have some better world in the other. The framing effect in behavioral economics shows that the lifting scheme can change with the way a question is posed or with psychological factors. This paper proves that such changes cannot be reduced to changes in preferences between possible worlds. Accordingly, we treat the lifting scheme as an independent dimension of evaluation and use a hybrid language to describe switches between lifting schemes. We thereby present a language for preference logic with dynamic lifting and prove its soundness and completeness.
tldr: This paper develops a dynamic preference logic that treats preference lifting schemes as independent evaluative dimensions and formalizes switches between them.
motivation: Preference lifting from possible worlds to propositions admits multiple schemes, and framing effects show these schemes can change independently of underlying world preferences, motivating a logic for dynamic lifting.
method: The author introduces a hybrid language to describe preference lifting and switches between lifting schemes, then proves soundness and completeness for the resulting dynamic preference logic.
result: The main result is a sound and complete axiomatization of the proposed dynamic preference logic of preference lifting.
conclusion: The work provides a formal framework for reasoning about changes in preference lifting schemes that cannot be reduced to changes in preferences between possible worlds.

title: Dynabase: A Database Of Extreme Examples In Arithmetic Dynamics
authors: Benjamin Hutz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Dynabase, a database cataloging extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics related to several major open conjectures: the Morton--Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture and the dynamical analogue of Lang's conjecture on canonical heights, as well as data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms. This database collects the known examples of extreme behavior for these problems and tracks the current status of subproblems based on degree and field of definition.
tldr: Dynabase is a curated database of extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics tied to open conjectures such as Morton–Silverman uniform boundedness and a dynamical Lang conjecture.
motivation: Arithmetic dynamics conjectures depend on sparse, scattered extreme examples, so a centralized record of known extremal cases and the status of degree/field-specific subproblems is needed.
method: The authors compile known extremal examples from the literature into a structured database, organizing entries by conjecture, degree, and field of definition, along with data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms.
result: The output is a queryable catalog of extreme examples and a status tracker for subproblems of the Morton–Silverman and dynamical Lang conjectures.
conclusion: Dynabase serves as a reference resource for number theorists working on arithmetic dynamics conjectures, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonholonomic Event-Triggered Source Seeking
authors: Victor Hugo Pereira Rodrigues, Tiago Roux Oliveira, Miroslav Krstic
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces an event-triggered source seeking control (ET-SSC) strategy for autonomous vehicles modeled as nonholonomic unicycles. The key feature of the proposed design is the separation between the continuous probing motion required for gradient extraction and the event-triggered update of the source-seeking correction. This separation enables aperiodic computation and transmission of the correction while the periodic probing signals remain continuously active. The triggering mechanism acts on a low-pass-filtered gradient estimate, obtained by high-pass (washout) filtering, demodulation, and low-pass filtering of the measured signal, and combines a relative and an absolute threshold. Stability is proved with a time-periodic Lyapunov function constructed along the exponentially stable periodic solution of the filtered closed loop, establishing practical exponential convergence of the vehicle to a neighborhood of the unknown source. The guaranteed minimum dwell time is strictly positive and independent of the probing frequency, which excludes Zeno behavior. Unlike available Lie-bracket analyses of the forward-velocity design, the proposed averaging-based analysis accommodates anisotropic quadratic source fields with distinct spatial curvatures. The resulting ET-SSC framework therefore provides a resource-aware implementation in which the source-seeking correction is updated aperiodically while the information-generating probing motion remains continuous.
tldr: The paper proposes an event-triggered source seeking control strategy for nonholonomic unicycle vehicles that separates continuous gradient-probing motion from aperiodic correction updates.
motivation: Autonomous vehicles seeking unknown sources typically require continuous computation and communication of control corrections, which is resource-intensive; an event-triggered scheme can reduce this burden while retaining convergence guarantees.
method: A low-pass-filtered gradient estimate is obtained via high-pass washout filtering, demodulation, and low-pass filtering of the measured signal, and a triggering rule combining relative and absolute thresholds updates the source-seeking correction aperiodically; stability is proved with a time-periodic Lyapunov function along the exponentially stable periodic solution.
result: Practical exponential convergence to a neighborhood of the unknown source is established, with a strictly positive guaranteed minimum dwell time independent of probing frequency (excluding Zeno behavior), and the averaging-based analysis handles anisotropic quadratic source fields with distinct spatial curvatures.
conclusion: The ET-SSC framework offers a resource-aware implementation where correction updates are aperiodic while information-generating probing remains continuous, extending beyond existing Lie-bracket analyses of forward-velocity designs.

title: A Column-Generation Approach To Length-Constrained Shortest Paths Under Cascading Causal Failures
authors: Nicol\`o Aicardi, Zuyuan Zhang, Sridhar Radhakrishnan, Kash Barker, Dritan Nace
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the study of cascading causal node failures, the failure of one set of nodes can trigger the failure of another, possibly non-adjacent, set, and these triggers can propagate in cascades. Given a graph, a set of causal failures, a source-terminal pair, and a constant [MATH], we study the length-constrained shortest-path problem of finding the maximum subset of causalities whose application preserves a source-terminal path of length at most [MATH] times the original distance. We show that the problem is NP-hard, a hardness that reflects the non-local, cascading nature of causal failures. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming formulation with explicit node-integrity variables that decouple the node state from routing, a column-generation algorithm built on a path-based reformulation whose pricing subproblem is solved by a three-level cascade (beam search, label-capped [MATH], and exact [MATH] with warm start), and a greedy heuristic as a fast baseline. On the IEEE 300 and Power 5000 benchmarks, all three methods are competitive. In dense synthetic networks of 10,000 to 15,000 nodes, the exact model exhausts its time budget or returns an order of magnitude fewer causalities, whereas column generation remains fast and accurate, emerging as the method of choice for large instances.
tldr: The paper studies a length-constrained shortest-path problem under cascading causal node failures and proposes a column-generation algorithm to maximize the set of causalities that can be applied while preserving a bounded source-terminal path.
motivation: Cascading causal failures in networks (e.g., infrastructure systems) can propagate non-locally, making resilience-aware routing hard; existing exact models do not scale to large graphs.
method: The authors prove NP-hardness, formulate a mixed-integer linear program with node-integrity variables, and develop a path-based column-generation algorithm whose pricing subproblem uses a three-level cascade (beam search, label-capped search, and exact search with warm start), plus a greedy heuristic baseline.
result: On IEEE 300 and Power 5000 benchmarks all three methods are competitive, while on dense synthetic networks of 10,000-15,000 nodes column generation remains fast and accurate whereas the exact model exhausts its time budget or returns far fewer causalities.
conclusion: Column generation is identified as the method of choice for large-scale instances of this resilience-oriented routing problem.

title: Inexact Proximal Method On Hadamard Manifolds
authors: M. S. Louzeiro, R. Serra, S. Vieira
abstract: ArXiv:2611.26873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze two inexact proximal point methods for unconstrained geodesically convex optimization on Hadamard manifolds. The first, a standard inexact proximal point method (SIPPM), accepts approximate subproblem solutions directly as new iterates and applies to arbitrary Hadamard manifolds under a summability condition on the relative error tolerances. The second, a hybrid inexact proximal point method (IHPPM), augments each inexact proximal step with a metric projection onto a half-space-like separating set, allowing the summability requirement to be relaxed to a fixed relative error tolerance at the cost of assuming geodesic convexity of the separating sets. For both methods we establish full asymptotic convergence, global [MATH] iteration-complexity bounds for approximate stationarity, and, under a local growth condition, local [MATH]-linear convergence rates---with [MATH]-superlinear acceleration for SIPPM when the proximal parameters tend to zero and a refined contraction factor for IHPPM. We further prove that the geodesic convexity of the separating sets holds automatically on Hadamard surfaces and on Hadamard manifolds of constant sectional curvature.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes inexact proximal point methods for geodesically convex optimization on Hadamard manifolds.
motivation: The authors aim to extend inexact proximal point algorithms to Riemannian optimization settings where subproblems are solved approximately.
method: Two methods are introduced: a standard inexact proximal point method and a hybrid variant with metric projection onto separating sets, with convergence and complexity analysis under geodesic convexity assumptions.
result: Both methods achieve asymptotic convergence and global iteration-complexity bounds, and local linear convergence is established under a growth condition with superlinear acceleration for one variant.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for inexact proximal methods on Hadamard manifolds, including conditions under which separating sets are geodesically convex.

title: On The Convergence Of Greedy Algorithms In One-dimensional Wasserstein Space
authors: Genevi\`eve Dusson, Carlo Marcati, Maximilian Penka
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the convergence of the greedy algorithm for approximating a compact set by barycenters in metric spaces, in particular in the space of one-dimensional measures endowed with the 2-Wasserstein distance. To this end, we compare several metric [MATH]-widths, which measure the best error achievable with [MATH]-point barycenters, using either classical barycenters having nonnegative weights or signed barycenters, with weights of arbitrary sign summing to one. For the analysis we exploit that quantile functions embed the one-dimensional 2-Wasserstein space isometrically into a convex cone of [MATH], and barycenter sets correspond to nonlinear projections of convex or affine hulls. We prove, both in the algebraic and exponential case, that the convergence rate of the greedy algorithm using signed barycenters matches the one of the metric [MATH]-width defined with classical barycenters. We provide counterexamples showing that this fails for the other combinations.
tldr: The paper analyzes convergence rates of greedy algorithms that approximate compact sets by barycenters in one-dimensional 2-Wasserstein space, comparing classical (nonnegative-weight) and signed barycenters via metric widths.
motivation: Greedy algorithms and barycenter-based approximation are widely used in reduced-order modeling and optimal transport numerics, but their convergence behavior in Wasserstein spaces is not well understood, particularly when signed barycenters are permitted.
method: Using the isometric embedding of the 1D 2-Wasserstein space into a convex cone of functions via quantile functions, barycenter sets are recast as nonlinear projections of convex or affine hulls, allowing several metric widths to be compared for algebraic and exponential convergence cases.
result: In both the algebraic and exponential regimes, the greedy algorithm with signed barycenters attains the same convergence rate as the metric width defined by classical barycenters; counterexamples show this equivalence fails for the remaining combinations.
conclusion: Signed barycenters are as powerful as classical barycenters for greedy approximation in 1D Wasserstein space, but the equivalence is delicate and depends on the specific pairing of algorithm and width.

title: Parareal Approximation Of Stochastic $L^2$-Boosting
authors: Duc-Quang Bui
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Parareal approximations of stochastic \(L^2\)-boosting, reusing the learner draws of the sequential algorithm in the fine propagators. We establish mean-square error bounds whose order improves with each correction, characterize the limiting distributions of normalized errors, including non-Gaussian components and the effects of coarse discretization, and derive sufficient conditions for preserving the statistical limit laws and validation-based stopping behavior of the sequential algorithm. Numerical experiments with sample-dependent coordinate and nonlinear residual-fitting learners examine the predicted convergence rates and limiting distributions, while computational benchmarks assess the efficiency of the method relative to sequential implementations.
tldr: The paper develops Parareal (parallel-in-time) approximations of stochastic L²-boosting, proving mean-square error bounds and characterizing the limiting distributions of the normalized errors.
motivation: Sequential boosting algorithms such as stochastic L²-boosting are computationally expensive because learner draws must be generated one after another; the authors aim to accelerate them by exploiting time-parallel integration techniques.
method: They apply the Parareal iteration to stochastic L²-boosting, reusing the same learner draws inside the fine propagators, and analyze the resulting scheme via mean-square error bounds, limiting-distribution theory, and conditions for preserving the statistical limit laws and validation-based stopping rules.
result: They obtain error bounds whose order improves with each Parareal correction, characterize the limiting distributions including non-Gaussian components and coarse-discretization effects, and confirm the predicted convergence rates and distributions in numerical experiments with coordinate-wise and nonlinear residual-fitting learners.
conclusion: Parareal acceleration preserves the statistical behavior of sequential stochastic L²-boosting under explicit sufficient conditions, offering efficiency gains that are benchmarked against sequential implementations.

title: Two-phase Visco-elastic Fene-p Model: Thermodynamically Consistent Modeling, Sharp Interface Limit Analysis And Unconditionally Energy Stable Numerical Scheme
authors: Dongdong He Yuzhe Qin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although mathematical modeling and numerical simulations for two-phase Newtonian flows have been extensively studied for many years, relatively little work has focused on developing thermodynamically consistent models for two-phase Non-Newtonian viscoelastic flows, and to the author's best konowledge, no structure-preserving numerical methods have been reported for such models. In this paper, we focus on modeling the two-phase non-Newtonnian visco-elastic FENE-P model based on the energetic variational approach (EnVarA). In the model, a phase-field function is introduced to describe the diffuse interface which satisfies the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) equation. And all the physical variables can be connected smoothly. We conduct a matched asymptotic analysis for the sharp interface limit, which shows the diffuse interface model will converge to the sharp interface model when the interface thickness trends to zero. We then reformulate the model in an equivalent form that facilitates the construction of the numerical scheme. A weakly decoupled scheme is proposed for the resulting FENE-P-CH system, and its unconditional energy stability is proved theoretically. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted to validate the model and assess the performance of the proposed scheme.
tldr: The paper develops a thermodynamically consistent phase-field model for two-phase viscoelastic FENE-P flows, analyzes its sharp-interface limit, and proposes an unconditionally energy-stable numerical scheme.
motivation: Thermodynamically consistent modeling and structure-preserving numerical methods for two-phase non-Newtonian viscoelastic flows are relatively underdeveloped compared with Newtonian flows.
method: The authors use an energetic variational approach with a Cahn-Hilliard phase field, perform matched asymptotic analysis for the sharp-interface limit, and construct a weakly decoupled unconditionally energy-stable scheme for the FENE-P-Cahn-Hilliard system.
result: The diffuse-interface model is shown to converge to a sharp-interface model as interface thickness vanishes, and numerical experiments validate the model and scheme performance.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamically consistent modeling and numerical framework for two-phase viscoelastic FENE-P flows, but it is a classical fluid mechanics and numerical analysis contribution rather than quantum information research.

title: A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method For Mesh-Free Pde Solvers And Its Error Analysis
authors: Yongcun Song, Shangzhi Zeng, Jin Zhang, Lvgang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mesh-free partial differential equation (PDE) solvers construct discrete systems from residuals at sampled points. These solvers fit coefficients in a parameterized trial representation and select solver-design parameters governing the representation, training-residual weighting, and regularization. These parameters strongly affect solution accuracy, yet existing selection strategies are largely tailored to particular solver classes. To address this limitation, we formulate a unified validation-driven bilevel optimization framework applicable across different solver classes, in which the lower level fits coefficients using training collocation residuals, while the upper level selects solver-design parameters using held-out validation residuals. For nonlinear PDEs, however, solving the nonlinear lower-level problem to high accuracy is costly, while the adjoint system is typically ill-conditioned and indefinite. To address this issue, we propose an efficient implicit hypergradient method that approximates the lower-level response using finite, warm-started damped Gauss-Newton (GN) updates. For the adjoint solve, we use the damped GN matrix to compute an initial adjoint and to precondition a finite number of minimum residual iterations. To quantify the errors introduced by these approximations, we derive local hypergradient error bounds that separate the contributions of the finite lower-level solve, adjoint damping, and the final adjoint residual. Combining this analysis with validation sampling bounds and residual stability, we relate validation residuals to PDE solution accuracy and establish error bounds for the computed PDE solution. Numerical experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across Kansa, random feature and extreme learning machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers.
tldr: The paper proposes a validation-driven bilevel optimization framework for selecting solver-design parameters in mesh-free PDE solvers, with hypergradient error bounds and PDE solution accuracy guarantees.
motivation: Design parameters in mesh-free PDE solvers strongly affect accuracy, but existing selection strategies are solver-class-specific and lack error quantification.
method: A bilevel formulation where the lower level fits coefficients on training collocation residuals and the upper level tunes design parameters via held-out validation residuals, solved with an efficient implicit hypergradient method using warm-started damped Gauss-Newton updates and preconditioned adjoint solves.
result: Local hypergradient error bounds decompose contributions from finite lower-level solves, adjoint damping, and adjoint residual, and combined with validation sampling bounds yield error bounds on the PDE solution; experiments on nonlinear and high-dimensional PDEs across Kansa, random feature/ELM, and PINN solvers confirm accuracy and efficiency.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified, theoretically grounded approach to parameter selection for mesh-free PDE solvers, though it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: A 3d PINN-Based Framework For Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
authors: Celia Taboada, Luis Nu\~nez, Ang\'elica Casero, Pedro Navas
abstract: ArXiv:2611.27351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance. Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. Validated on 2D canonical channels (steady and pulsatile, with and without RCR outlet), the framework is then applied to a patient-specific right pulmonary artery, reproducing outlet flow, mean pressure, and the velocity and dynamic pressure fields with errors on the order of the data resolution.
